Questions: Name the economic term that describes how much of a good or service a producer is willing and able to produce at different prices.
A market has two halves. The buyers' half is demand — what's the sellers' half called?
This economic term describes how much of a good or service a producer is willing and able to produce at different prices.
Name the economic term that describes property owned by individuals or companies, not by the government or by the people as a whole.
Not owned by the government, not owned by everybody. So owned by whom?
This economic term describes property owned by individuals or companies, not by the government or by the people as a whole.
Name the economic term for a person, such as Bill Gates or Oprah Winfrey, who organizes, manages, and takes on the risks of a business.
What do you call someone who starts a business and carries the risk themselves?
This economic term names a person, such as Bill Gates or Oprah Winfrey, who organizes, manages, and takes on the risks of a business.
Name the term that describes the government's constitutional power to take private property for public use as long as the owner is paid fair compensation.
They pay you fairly, but you can't say no. Two words; the second is “domain.”
This term describes the government’s constitutional power to take private property for public use as long as the owner is paid fair compensation.
Name the economic term that describes a situation in which unlimited wants exceed the limited resources available to fulfill those wants.
Wants are unlimited, resources are not. One word for that gap.
This economic term describes a situation in which unlimited wants exceed the limited resources available to fulfill those wants.
Name the economic term that describes an amount of money borrowed by someone that must be repaid, usually with interest.
Borrowed money you pay back with interest — the plain everyday word.
This economic term describes an amount of money borrowed by someone that must be repaid, usually with interest.
Identify the city and state where the Civil War started in 1861 when Confederate forces led by General Beauregard (bow-ree-gard) fired upon it.
Think Fort Sumter. Which South Carolina port is it in?
In 1861 Confederate forces led by General Beauregard fired on this city, starting the Civil War.
State the nickname used by Americans for the British soldiers stationed in America during the Revolutionary War.
It's about the color of their coats.
Americans used this nickname for the British soldiers stationed in America during the Revolutionary War.
Identify the two countries where the US engaged in the “War on Terror” after the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
One was invaded in 2001, the other in 2003.
After the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, the US engaged in the “War on Terror” in these two countries.
Previously an actor portraying the president on a popular fictional Ukrainian television show, this man was actually elected President of Ukraine in April of 2019.
He played a fictional president on TV before the real job. Surname starts with Z.
On June 1, 2017, President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from this accord, focused on climate change mitigation.
Named for the city where it was signed, and it's about the climate.
On May 24, 2019, she announced her resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
The UK's second woman Prime Minister, after Thatcher.
On December 6, 2017, President Donald Trump announced the recognition of this city as the capital of Israel, where the US embassy was eventually relocated months later.
Israel's government sits there, though most embassies were in Tel Aviv.
This acclaimed architect, who designed the Louvre Pyramid, died on May 16, 2019, at the age of 102.
Chinese-American architect known by two initials and a short surname.
Prior to his death on January 13, 2019, Alfred K. Newman was one of the last survivors of this group, whose indecipherable code contributed to the Allies' victory in World War II.
Their code was a Native American language the Axis never broke.
Following a referendum on June 23, 2016, this country voted to leave the European Union.
The vote was nicknamed Brexit. What does the B stand for?
Lasting from December 22, 2018 to January 25, 2019, this occurred and was the longest in U.S. government history.
35 days over the winter holidays. What stops when Congress and the President can't agree on funding?
Lasting from December 22, 2018 to January 25, 2019, this was the longest one in U.S. government history.
The Athenians led by Miltiades forced the Persians back to their ships in this 490 BCE victory, which legendarily inspired Pheidippides to run 26 miles with news of the battle.
A modern running race is named after the place this was fought.
Name the Roman emperor who ordered the death of his mother, may have kicked his wife to death, poisoned his stepbrother, and reputedly fiddled while Rome burned before he committed suicide.
He supposedly played music while the city burned.
This Roman emperor ordered the death of his mother, may have kicked his wife to death, poisoned his stepbrother, and reputedly fiddled while Rome burned before he committed suicide.

In the third century BCE, Ptolemy I established a facility in which scholars copied, revised, and edited works of classical Greek writers. At its height it held about 500,000 papyrus scrolls before it was destroyed by fire. Give the location of this library in Egypt.
The great library sat in the Egyptian port city Alexander founded.

In the third century BCE, Ptolemy I established a library here in which scholars copied, revised, and edited works of classical Greek writers; it held about 500,000 papyrus scrolls before fire destroyed it.
If you wanted to visit the world's oldest parliamentary institution, you would want to see the Althing, located 45 kilometers east of the capital Reykjavik in this European island country.
State the first and last name of the president of South Africa who died in December of 2013 after a world-changing life.
He spent 27 years in prison before he became president.
This president of South Africa died in December of 2013 after a world-changing life.
Name the modern-day country where Ferdinand Magellan landed on 16 March 1521 thinking he had arrived in the Spice Islands. He would be killed by its natives a month later.
He died in the islands Spain later named for King Philip II.
Ferdinand Magellan landed in this modern-day country on 16 March 1521 thinking he had reached the Spice Islands; its natives killed him a month later.
This “window to the west” city lies on the Neva River near the Gulf of Finland. It was formerly known as Leningrad and contains the Winter Palace and the Hermitage Museum. Name this Russian city.
Named for a saint and a founding tsar. The Soviets called it Leningrad.
This “window to the west” Russian city lies on the Neva River near the Gulf of Finland, was formerly known as Leningrad, and holds the Winter Palace and the Hermitage Museum.

This philosopher's theory that the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government should be separated inspired America's founding fathers. Name this French author of The Spirit of the Laws.
French, Enlightenment, wrote about separating the powers. Starts with M.
This French author of The Spirit of the Laws argued that the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government should be separated, inspiring America’s founding fathers.

In April 1986, an explosion and fire at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in the Soviet Union made it the site of the worst nuclear disaster in history. Name the modern-day country where you would find the 30-kilometer-wide “zone of alienation” today.
Chernobyl is about 60 miles north of Kyiv.
The 1986 Chernobyl explosion was the worst nuclear disaster in history, and its 30-kilometer-wide “zone of alienation” sits in this modern-day country.
Name the scientist who discovered that the ratio of the electromotive force to the current in a circuit is constant. This unit is named after him.
The unit of electrical resistance carries his name.
This scientist discovered that the ratio of the electromotive force to the current in a circuit is constant, and the unit is named after him.
Identify the month that Congressional elections are held in even-numbered years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday.
Election Day is always in the fall.
Congressional elections are held in this month in even-numbered years, on the first Tuesday after the first Monday.
List the three branches of the US government.
One writes the laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.
These are the three branches of the US government.
Identify the two US states that form the northern border of Florida.
These two US states form the northern border of Florida.

Newton's First Law of Motion states that objects in motion remain in motion unless acted upon by an outside force, and objects at rest stay at rest unless acted upon by an outside force. This statement is also referred to as the law of what?
An object's resistance to any change in its motion. One word.
Newton’s First Law of Motion — objects in motion remain in motion and objects at rest stay at rest unless acted upon by an outside force — is also called the law of this.
Sara jumped off her rowboat into the lake. As she pushed her body forward, the boat moved backwards. Identify which of Newton's three laws best describes the motion of Sara and her boat.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Which law is that?
the Law of Conservation of Mass
Sara jumped off her rowboat into the lake, and as she pushed her body forward the boat moved backwards; this one of Newton’s three laws best describes that motion.
Describe the difference between reflection and refraction.
Reflection is the change in direction of waves when they bounce off a barrier. Refraction is the change in direction of waves as they pass from one medium to another.
One bounces off a surface; the other bends going through into something new.
State the scientific term for the process in which a substance goes directly from a solid to a gaseous state.
Solid straight to gas, skipping liquid. The reverse of deposition.
This is the scientific term for the process in which a substance goes directly from a solid to a gaseous state.
Of silver, zinc, and iron, which would appear last on the Periodic Table with the highest atomic number?
Later on the table means a bigger atomic number. Which sits furthest along?
they all have the same atomic number
Of silver, zinc, and iron, this one appears last on the Periodic Table, with the highest atomic number.
Of neon, nitrogen, and oxygen, which is the lightest and would appear first on the Periodic Table with the lowest atomic number?
Lightest means fewest protons. One of these has just 7.
they all have the same atomic number
Of neon, nitrogen, and oxygen, this one is the lightest and appears first on the Periodic Table, with the lowest atomic number.
State the electrical charge of the following particles: proton, neutron, and electron.
proton = positive charge; neutron = neutral charge; electron = negative charge
The particle named for being neutral gives itself away; electrons are the negative ones.
Name the biological process where a single cell divides twice to produce four daughter cells.
Mitosis divides once into two. This one divides twice into four, and it makes sex cells.
In this biological process a single cell divides twice to produce four daughter cells.
Name the process by which living things with beneficial traits tend to survive and reproduce more than individuals with other, less successful traits.
Darwin's central idea — nature does the choosing, not people.
By this process, living things with beneficial traits tend to survive and reproduce more than individuals with other, less successful traits.
Describe the difference between Darwin's Natural Selection and Artificial Selection.
Natural selection is the process by which living things with beneficial traits tend to survive; artificial selection is when humans breed plants and animals to have useful traits.
The difference is who does the selecting.
Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when one member of the association benefits while the other is harmed.
One wins, one loses. Think of a tick on a dog.
This type of symbiotic relationship takes place when one member of the association benefits while the other is harmed.
Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when both organisms benefit from the relationship.
Both win. Think of a bee and a flower.
This type of symbiotic relationship takes place when both organisms benefit from the relationship.
Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when one organism benefits while the other neither benefits nor is harmed.
One wins, the other doesn't care either way. Think of a barnacle on a whale.
This type of symbiotic relationship takes place when one organism benefits while the other neither benefits nor is harmed.
Identify the type of land mammal, excluding humans, known to have the longest average lifespan at slightly over 60 years.
A land mammal, very large, famous for its memory.
Excluding humans, this land mammal has the longest average lifespan, at slightly over 60 years.

Identify the serious respiratory illness that is highly contagious and can be fatal. The first case was reported in Vietnam in February 2003. It spread rapidly across Southeast Asia, as well as China, Canada, and the US.
A four-letter acronym. The first S stands for Severe.

This serious respiratory illness is highly contagious and can be fatal; the first case was reported in Vietnam in February 2003, and it spread rapidly across Southeast Asia as well as China, Canada, and the US.
Describe the difference between lava with high or low concentrations of silica.
Lava with a low concentration of silica is thin and runny. Lava with high concentrations of silica is very thick.
Silica is what makes lava thick or thin — decide which way it goes.
Explain the cause of day and night on the earth.
rotation of the earth on its axis
The Earth spins once every 24 hours. What is spinning called?
the earth's revolution around the sun
the tilt of the earth's axis
the moon's orbit around the earth
This motion of the earth is the cause of day and night.
State how many commas are needed in the following sentence, then identify where they should be placed: “They planned a route and they prepared their equipment.”
Two independent clauses joined by “and” take a comma before the “and.”
none; the sentence is already correct
The sentence “They planned a route and they prepared their equipment” needs this many commas.
List the three common types of figurative language.
Two of the three compare things — one directly, one using “like” or “as.” The third gives human traits to something that isn't human.
These are the three common types of figurative language.
Written by Canadian author Margaret Atwood in 2019, The Testaments is the sequel to what dystopian novel originally published in 1985 that was later adapted into a popular Hulu television series?
Atwood's 1985 novel set in Gilead, later a Hulu series.
Written by Canadian author Margaret Atwood in 2019, The Testaments is the sequel to this 1985 dystopian novel, later adapted into a popular Hulu series.
Why would historians consider “The Autobiography of Theodore Roosevelt” to be a primary source?
The work is created by the author; it's from the time period of its subject; there is no modern commentary or criticism.
Ask who wrote it, and whether they lived through what they're describing.
The following is what type of writing? “Should schools ban cell-phones?”
It's a “should” question with two sides you could take.
“Should schools ban cell-phones?” is a prompt for this type of writing.
The following is what type of writing? “Should student-athletes be required to pass all classes before being permitted to play?”
Same shape as the cell-phone question — a “should” question with two sides.
“Should student-athletes be required to pass all classes before being permitted to play?” is a prompt for this type of writing.
The following is what type of writing? “The Journey of a Butterfly”
It's teaching you facts about something real.
“The Journey of a Butterfly” is a title for this type of writing.
The following is what type of writing? “Goldilocks and the Three Bears”
It tells a story with characters.
“Goldilocks and the Three Bears” is a piece of this type of writing.
Name the builder of the house in the following nursery rhyme: “This is the cat / That killed the rat / That ate the malt / That lay in the house…”
In the nursery rhyme “This is the cat / That killed the rat / That ate the malt / That lay in the house…,” this man built the house.
Correct the error in the following sentence: “Although they lost the game, they still felt good about theirselves.”
There is no such word as “theirselves.” What's the real reflexive pronoun?
In “Although they lost the game, they still felt good about theirselves,” this word belongs in place of “theirselves.”
Identify the helping verb and the main verb in the following sentence: “Will you see him again?”
helping verb = will; main verb = see
Split “Will…see.” One verb helps; the other carries the meaning.
Identify and correct the error in the following sentence: “She liked to stroll in the woods and hearing the birds sing.”
parallelism; change to “to stroll…and to hear” or “strolling…and hearing”
The two things in the list don't have matching forms — one is “to stroll,” the other ends in -ing.
Give the verb tense of the following sentence: “Brandon had a difficult time deciding on what to order from the menu.”
“Had” plus a past participle. That still lands in the past.
“Brandon had a difficult time deciding on what to order from the menu” is written in this verb tense.
Give the proper nouns contained in the following sentence: “She wanted to know what the best route to take to get to the San Francisco Bridge was in order to take a boat cruise.”
Proper nouns name one specific thing and get capitalized. “Route” and “cruise” don't.
“She wanted to know what the best route to take to get to the San Francisco Bridge was in order to take a boat cruise” contains this proper noun.
Change the following sentence from present tense to future tense: “The sisters are throwing a barbecue for the holiday weekend.”
The sisters will be throwing a barbecue for the holiday weekend.
Right now it's “are throwing.” Add “will” to push it forward.
The sisters threw a barbecue for the holiday weekend.
The sisters have thrown a barbecue for the holiday weekend.
The sisters are going to a barbecue for the holiday weekend.
This is “The sisters are throwing a barbecue for the holiday weekend,” moved from present tense into future tense.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “mar” as used in words like “submarine” and “marina.”
Submarine, marina, mariner, maritime — where do all of those happen?
Words like “submarine” and “marina” carry this Latin root meaning sea or ocean.
Define the word “shatter” as used in the following sentence: “I saw the vase shatter when it fell from the shelf.”
The vase hit the floor. What did it do?
In “I saw the vase shatter when it fell from the shelf,” this verb means to break into several pieces.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “super” as used in words like “supersonic” and “superior.”
above, higher, or more in quality or quantity
Supersonic is faster than sound; a superior is higher up.
under, below, or lower in position or rank
fast, quick, or sudden in movement or speed
around, surrounding, or encircling on all sides
Words like “supersonic” and “superior” carry this Latin root meaning above, higher, or greater in quality or quantity.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “ver” as used in words like “verify” and “veracity.”
To verify something is to check that it's ___.
Words like “verify” and “veracity” carry this Latin root meaning true or truth.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “tox” as used in words like “toxin” and “toxic.”
Words like “toxin” and “toxic” carry this Latin root meaning poison or deadly.

Give the word of Arabic origin that was first used to describe the cost of merchandise damaged at sea. It now is used to describe something ordinary or unexceptional, the middle or typical number of a list of numbers, or an arithmetic mean.
It started as damaged cargo at sea; now it means the middle of a list of numbers.
This word of Arabic origin first described the cost of merchandise damaged at sea; it now describes something ordinary or unexceptional, or the arithmetic mean of a list of numbers.

Give the five-letter word of Arabic origin that describes a thin, translucent fabric with a loose or open weave. When woven from silk, it was used in clothing. Now it is more commonly made from cotton and used in medical dressings and bandages.
Five letters, thin and see-through, and it's in every first aid kit.

This five-letter word of Arabic origin names a thin, translucent fabric with a loose or open weave; once woven from silk for clothing, it is now usually cotton and used in medical dressings and bandages.
“Jumbo shrimp,” “friendly fire,” and “original copy” are examples of what figure of speech, in which seemingly contradictory terms appear in conjunction?
Two words that contradict each other, put together on purpose.
“Jumbo shrimp,” “friendly fire,” and “original copy” are examples of this figure of speech, in which seemingly contradictory terms appear together.
Don't solve for x. 7x + 2 = 28 means 7x = 26 — and the question only wants 7x minus 1.
If 7x + 2 = 28, this is the value of 7x − 1.
Calculate the value of 2x² + 3y² − 4x + 2y − 17 when x = 3 and y = −2.
Substitute first, then do the exponents before the multiplying. y is negative, so y² comes out positive.
This is the value of 2x² + 3y² − 4x + 2y − 17 when x = 3 and y = −2.
6³ = 216 and 6² = 36. Clear the parentheses first, then subtract 7 × 36.
Ellen's favorite lotion costs $3.00 for 4 fluid ounces. At that same rate, calculate what she would pay for a quart of lotion if a quart is equal to 32 fluid ounces.
Find the price per ounce and multiply by 32 — or notice that 32 is 8 × 4.
Ellen’s favorite lotion costs $3.00 for 4 fluid ounces; at that same rate, this is what she would pay for a quart, or 32 fluid ounces.
Determine at what point on a graph the lines y = 2x − 1 and y = 3x − 5 will cross.
They cross where the two y values are equal. Set 2x − 1 = 3x − 5, solve for x, then plug back in.
The lines y = 2x − 1 and y = 3x − 5 cross at this point on a graph.
Nancy is knitting a baby blanket that requires 750 meters of yarn. There are 180 meters of yarn in each ball. Determine how many balls of yarn Nancy must buy to make sure she has enough yarn.
Divide 750 by 180, then round UP — you can't buy part of a ball.
Nancy’s baby blanket needs 750 meters of yarn and each ball holds 180 meters, so she must buy this many balls to be sure she has enough.

Freddy reads 30 pages of his book on the first day. The next day he reads another 36 pages. On the third day, he reads another 42 pages. If he continues to increase the number of pages he reads each day by 6, how many days will it take him to read a book that has 270 pages?
The days go 30, 36, 42, 48… Keep a running total and stop when you pass 270.
Freddy reads 30 pages the first day, 36 the next, and 42 on the third, increasing by 6 pages a day; a 270-page book takes him this long.
State the term for an integer greater than 1 whose only positive factors are 1 and itself.
Its only factors are 1 and itself: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11…
This is the term for an integer greater than 1 whose only positive factors are 1 and itself.
Arrange the digits 8, 2, 3, 5, 9 to a) make the largest number possible; b) state the place value of the digit 8 in the number; c) state whether this number is divisible by 2, 3, 4, 5.
a) 98,532; b) thousand(s); c) divisible by 2, 3, and 4, not by 5
Biggest digits first. Then count places from the right — ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. For divisibility check the last digit, the digit sum, and the last two digits.
If Kayla left a $10.47 tip on a dinner that cost $87.25, what percentage did she leave her waiter?
Part over whole: 10.47 ÷ 87.25, then move the decimal two places.
Kayla left a $10.47 tip on a dinner that cost $87.25, which works out to this percentage.
Calculate the common fraction that is halfway between the fractions 1/5 and 1/4, then reduce your answer.
Halfway between two numbers is their average. Give them a common denominator of 20 first.
Reduced, this common fraction is exactly halfway between 1/5 and 1/4.

A phone company charges $2 for the first five minutes of an international phone call and 30 cents per minute thereafter. If Malik makes a phone call that lasts 25 minutes, calculate the total cost of the phone call.
The $2 covers the first 5 minutes. That leaves 20 minutes at 30 cents each.
A phone company charges $2 for the first five minutes of an international call and 30 cents a minute after that, so Malik’s 25-minute call costs this.
Brian paid his gym a one-time registration fee of $30 for boxing lessons. Additionally, he paid $20 per lesson. Determine the total amount he paid if he took seven lessons.
One flat fee plus a per-lesson cost: 30 + 20 × 7.
Brian paid his gym a one-time $30 registration fee plus $20 per boxing lesson, so seven lessons cost him this in total.
Calculate in hours and minutes the amount of time John worked if he started at 7:35 a.m. and worked until 1:20 p.m. on the same day.
Count up to noon first, then past it — the shift crosses 12:00.
John started work at 7:35 a.m. and worked until 1:20 p.m. the same day — this long, in hours and minutes.
Calculate the cost to fence the garden if fencing costs $0.35 per foot and the area of a square garden is 289 square feet.
A square's area is side × side, so the side is √289. You need the perimeter, not the area.
A square garden covers 289 square feet and fencing runs $0.35 per foot, so fencing it costs this.
Jamie worked three hours on Monday, four hours on Tuesday, six hours on Thursday, and one hour on Friday; how many total minutes did Jamie work?
Add the hours first, then convert once at the end by multiplying by 60.
Jamie worked three hours Monday, four Tuesday, six Thursday, and one Friday — this many minutes in all.
Tammy spent 55 minutes watching Stranger Things, 95 minutes watching Riverdale, and 35 minutes watching 13 Reasons Why; how many total minutes did Tammy spend watching Netflix?
Straight addition — the answer is already in minutes, so nothing to convert.
Tammy spent 55 minutes on Stranger Things, 95 on Riverdale, and 35 on 13 Reasons Why — this many minutes of Netflix in all.
In a gaming club consisting of 80 members, one-fourth of them are boys. If no one leaves the club, what is the minimum number of boys that would need to join to make the club one-third boys?
A quarter of 80 is 20 boys. Set (20 + x)/(80 + x) = 1/3; the new boys grow both the top and the bottom.
A gaming club of 80 members is one-fourth boys; with no one leaving, this many boys would have to join to make it one-third boys.
Calculate, rounding to the nearest tenth, the volume of a cylindrical can which has a diameter of six centimeters and a height of six centimeters.
Volume = π × r² × h. The diameter is 6, so the radius is 3.
Rounded to the nearest tenth, this is the volume of a cylindrical can six centimeters across and six centimeters tall.
Determine the type of angle that ABC is if its measure is 67 degrees.
Under 90° is one thing, exactly 90° another, over 90° a third.
Angle ABC measures 67 degrees, making it this type of angle.
Calculate the number of possible combinations of who will serve as greeter during a four-night period if each night, either Amy or Matthew (but not both) serves as greeter at the door.
Two choices each night, four nights: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2.
For four nights running, either Amy or Matthew — but not both — serves as greeter at the door; this is the number of possible combinations.
Stacy has 6 identical black socks and 5 identical white socks in a drawer. If she selects without looking, determine how many socks she must take from the drawer to be sure of having a matching pair.
Worst case, she pulls one of each color first. What does the very next sock guarantee?
Stacy has 6 identical black socks and 5 identical white socks in a drawer, so selecting without looking she must take this many to be sure of a matching pair.

Mr. Green, Mr. Red, and Mr. Blue were waiting at a bus stop. One man wore a red suit, one a green suit, and the other a blue suit. “Isn't it odd,” said the man in the blue suit, “that our suits have colors corresponding to our names, but not one of us is wearing a suit that matches our name?” Mr. Red looked at the other two and said, “you're absolutely correct.” Determine what color suit each man is wearing.
Mr. Red = green suit, Mr. Blue = red suit, Mr. Green = blue suit
Nobody wears their own color. Start from the fact that Mr. Red answered the man in the blue suit, so Mr. Red isn't in blue.

Explain how you could throw a ball as hard as you can and have it come back to you without it striking or bouncing off anything. There is nothing attached to it, and no one else catches it or throws it back to you.
Throw the ball straight up into the air.
Gravity brings it back down. Which direction do you throw it?
Throw it into a strong headwind.
Throw it and run to catch it.
With nothing attached to it and no one else catching it, you can throw a ball as hard as you can and still have it come back to you by doing this.

A Petri dish hosts a healthy colony of bacteria. Once a minute, every bacterium divides into two. The colony was founded by a single cell at noon. At exactly 12:43 the Petri dish was half full. At what time will the dish be full?
It doubles every minute. If it's half full now, how long until it doubles once?
Bacteria in a Petri dish double every minute, starting from a single cell at noon; the dish was half full at 12:43, so it is full at this time.
A study of 100 boys and 100 girls found that 60% of girls and 20% of boys enjoy the game Zombie Death. What percent of the children in the study who enjoy Zombie Death are girls?
60 girls and 20 boys enjoy it — 80 kids in all. What fraction of 80 is 60?
In a study of 100 boys and 100 girls, 60% of the girls and 20% of the boys enjoy Zombie Death, so this percent of the children who enjoy it are girls.

Twenty people each competed in a scavenger hunt. Twenty percent of the people each found 80% of the items, and 80% of the people each found 20% of the items. Those who found the most items found a dozen items each. How many items were on the list?
The top group each found 80% of the list, and that came to 12 items. So 12 is 80% of what?
Twenty people competed in a scavenger hunt: 20% of them each found 80% of the items, 80% each found 20%, and the top finders found a dozen apiece — this many items were on the list.
Jeff is younger than Rodney but older than Debbie. Larry is older than Erica who is older than Jeff. Rodney is older than Larry. Name the middle child in this grouping.
Line all five up youngest to oldest, then take the middle one.
Jeff is younger than Rodney but older than Debbie; Larry is older than Erica, who is older than Jeff; and Rodney is older than Larry. This is the middle child.
Determine the probability that a person selected at random is less than 20 years old if, in a group of 120 people, 90 are more than 30 years old and all others are less than 20 years old.
120 total, 90 are over 30, so the rest are under 20. Part over whole, then reduce.
In a group of 120 people, 90 are over 30 years old and the rest are under 20, making this the probability that a person selected at random is under 20.

There are 5 blue marbles, 4 red marbles, and 3 yellow marbles in a box. If Jim randomly selects a marble from the box, calculate the probability of selecting a red or yellow marble. State your answer as a fraction.
Red plus yellow over the total — and the total includes the blue ones.
A box holds 5 blue, 4 red, and 3 yellow marbles, so this fraction is the probability Jim draws a red or a yellow one.

Tommy randomly selects a card from a standard deck of 52 playing cards. Calculate the percent probability that his chosen card shows a red number greater than 6. Express your answer to the nearest hundredth.
Red cards only, and “number greater than 6” means 7, 8, 9, 10. Face cards and aces are not numbers.
To the nearest hundredth, this is the percent probability that a card drawn from a standard 52-card deck shows a red number greater than 6.
At Andre's party, every person there shakes hands with each other once, and there are 45 handshakes. Calculate how many people are at Andre's party.
Each pair shakes once: n(n − 1) ÷ 2 = 45. Try small numbers until it fits.
Everyone at Andre’s party shakes hands with everyone else exactly once, for 45 handshakes — this many people are there.
A drawer contains five socks: two black and three blue. Determine the probability that two socks pulled out of the drawer at random will match. Express your answer as a common fraction.
Both black, or both blue. Count the ways for each, out of the 10 possible pairs.
A drawer holds five socks, two black and three blue; as a common fraction, this is the probability that two pulled at random match.
If Sally has 3 pairs of pants and 4 shirts, and an outfit consists of 1 pair of pants and 1 shirt, how many distinct outfits can Sally make?
Every pair of pants goes with every shirt: 3 × 4.
Sally has 3 pairs of pants and 4 shirts, and an outfit is one of each, so she can make this many distinct outfits.

A basket of fruit contains 5 oranges, 4 apples, and 6 bananas. If you choose a piece of fruit randomly from the basket, what is the probability that it will be a banana? State your answer as a common fraction.
Bananas over all the fruit — add all three kinds for the bottom.
A basket holds 5 oranges, 4 apples, and 6 bananas; as a common fraction, this is the probability of randomly choosing a banana.

In a box of 24 crayons, there are exactly four that are shades of blue. If Nick selects one crayon at random from the full box, what is the probability that he will select a crayon that is a shade of blue? State your answer as a common fraction.
Blue crayons over all the crayons, then reduce 4/24.
Exactly four of the 24 crayons in a full box are shades of blue; as a common fraction, this is the probability Nick draws a blue one.
Match each parent rock with what it becomes: Parent rock: limestone; shale; granite; coal; sandstone Becomes: gneiss; slate; marble; quartzite; anthracite coal
Heat and pressure turn each one into the next. Which soft one becomes the shiny white stone sculptors love?
List the steps an igneous rock must undergo to become a sedimentary rock.
Answers may vary: Igneous rock---->undergoes weathering and erosion----->becomes sediment---->sediment is compacted and cemented into sedimentary rock
Weather it, move it, pile it, squeeze it. Four steps, in that order.

Two objects on Earth are dropped from the top of a building that is 70 meters high. Object A has a mass of 12 g and object B has a mass of 6 kg. Assuming there is no air resistance, which object will hit the ground first?
Both objects hit the ground at the same time
Gravity pulls on both the same way. Mass is a red herring here.
Object B, because it is heavier
Object A, because it is lighter
Object B, because it has more momentum
Object A has a mass of 12 g and object B a mass of 6 kg, and both are dropped from a 70-meter building with no air resistance — this is what happens.
List the four bases that make up the ladder of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
Two of the four pair with each other and the other two do the same. One tile belongs to RNA rather than DNA, and two are rails of the ladder, not rungs.
Two stores selling tires have opened up in a small town. Explain at least two ways in which these stores might engage in competition to gain more customers for themselves.

Answers may vary: stores might reduce prices for a time [sales], offer incentives [buy one-get one free, raffles, contests, etc.], offer exclusive products not found in the other store, hold events that demonstrate exemplary service, etc.
Think about what a store can change: the price, what it throws in free, or what only it sells.

State the term that means: a) land completely surrounded by water; b) land surrounded on three sides by water; c) a narrow inlet of the sea bordered by steep cliffs; d) a narrow waterway connecting two larger bodies of water
a) island; b) peninsula; c) fjord; d) strait
Island, peninsula, fjord, strait — but which is which? (c) is the one carved by a glacier.

Match each dictator to the country he once controlled: Dictators: Idi Amin; Fidel Castro; Adolf Hitler; Benito Mussolini; Pol Pot; Joseph Stalin Countries: Cambodia; Germany; Cuba; Uganda; Italy; Russia
Amin - Uganda, Castro - Cuba, Hitler - Germany, Mussolini - Italy, Pot - Cambodia, Stalin - Russia
Amin ran an African country; Pot ran a Southeast Asian one. The two European ones are the famous pair.
Starting with the earliest, arrange the following states in chronological order according to when they joined the Union: Florida; Kansas; Ohio; New Jersey; Rhode Island
New Jersey (1787), Rhode Island (1790), Ohio (1803), Florida (1845), Kansas (1861)
Two of these were among the original thirteen colonies, so they go first. Kansas was a Civil War flashpoint — it goes last.
Starting with the earliest, arrange the following states in chronological order according to when they joined the Union: California; Georgia; Illinois; Kentucky; Utah; Washington
Georgia (1788), Kentucky (1792), Illinois (1818), California (1850), Washington (1889), Utah (1896)
Georgia was one of the original thirteen. The two youngest here are both far west, and one waited until 1896.
Explain at least two differences between inflation and recession in a given economy.

Answers may vary: During inflation, prices for goods and services rise and the value of money falls because too much money is in circulation, interest rates increase, banks tend to loan less, etc. During recession, demand for goods and services decreases, economic growth slows, people tend to save money rather than spend, unemployment increases, interest rates decrease, banks want to increase investment, etc.
One is about prices going up. The other is about the whole economy slowing down.
Explain at least two differences between a market economy and a command economy.

Answers may vary: Market economies rely on consumer behaviors to determine how goods are produced and at what prices, with very little government control over private property and means of production, etc. Command economies have government control of resources and means of production, price controls, less consumer input, etc.
One kind of economy lets shoppers decide. The other lets the government decide.

Match the symbiotic relationship with the correct definition: Relationships: Mutualism; Commensalism; Parasitism Definitions: One organism is harmed while the other benefits; both organisms benefit; One organism benefits while the other neither benefits or is harmed
Mutualism-both organisms benefit; Commensalism-one organism benefits while the other neither benefits or is harmed; Parasitism-one organism is harmed while the other benefits
Mutual means shared, so both win. A parasite always harms its host. That leaves the middle one.

Answer the following questions about Charles, who takes a Ping-Pong ball & a golf ball onto the garage roof and drops them both into a pan of water on the driveway. 1) Identify the kind of energy that the balls have as they fall and hit the water; 2) Compare the acceleration of the 2 balls; 3) Explain why the golf ball makes a bigger splash.
1) Kinetic energy; 2) The acceleration of two balls in the same; 3) The more massive golf balls with the same acceleration have more kinetic energy.
Falling objects have energy of motion. And a heavier ball carries more of it at the same speed.

Match the Supreme Court case to the part of the Constitution that was used to justify the Court’s decision: Cases: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka; Fletcher v. Peck; Gibbons v. Ogden; Johnson v. McIntosh; McCulloch v. Maryland Constitution: “supremacy clause”; “equal protection clause”; “discovery doctrine”; “contract clause”; “commerce clause”
Brown - equal protection, Fletcher - contract clause, Gibbons - commerce clause, Johnson - discovery doctrine, McCulloch - supremacy clause
Brown was about schools treating people unequally. McCulloch was about federal law beating state law.

Match the Supreme Court case to the Bill of Rights amendment it served to clarify: Cases: Atkins v. Virginia; Gideon v. Wainwright; Mapp v. Ohio; Miranda v. Arizona; Texas v. Johnson Amendments: 1st, 4th, 5th, 6th, 8th Amendments
Miranda is about self-incrimination, Gideon about a lawyer, Mapp about searches, Atkins about punishment, Johnson about flag burning.

Match each former country name to its new name: Old Name: British Honduras; Ceylon; Dutch East Indies; East Pakistan; Formosa; Zaire New Name: Bangladesh; Belize; Democratic Republic of Congo; Indonesia; Sri Lanka; Taiwan
British Honduras - Belize, Ceylon - Sri Lanka, Dutch East Indies - Indonesia, East Pakistan - Bangladesh, Formosa - Taiwan, Zaire - Democratic Republic of Congo
Ceylon still grows the tea. Formosa is an island off China. Zaire is in central Africa.

Match each ancient city to the current-day country where you would find it today: Cities: Alexandria; Antioch; Athens; Jaisalmer; Rome; Samarkand; Tyre Countries: Egypt; Greece; India; Italy; Lebanon; Turkey; Uzbekistan
Alexandria - Egypt, Antioch - Turkey, Athens - Greece, Jaisalmer - India; Rome - Italy, Samarkand - Uzbekistan, Tyre - Lebanon
Alexandria was Egypt's great port. Samarkand was on the Silk Road in Central Asia. Tyre was Phoenician.

Match each region conquered by the Roman Empire to the current-day country where it exists today: Areas: Britannia; Cappadocia; Gallia, Gaul; Hispania; Macedonia; Mauretania; Thracia Countries: Bulgaria; England; France; Greece; Morocco; Spain; Turkey
Britannia - England, Cappadocia - Turkey, Gallia or Gaul - France, Hispania - Spain, Macedonia - Greece, Mauretania - Morocco, Thracia - Bulgaria
Britannia and Hispania nearly say themselves. Gaul is Caesar's; Thracia is on the Black Sea.
Match each river to the ancient city that emerged along it: Rivers: Euphrates; Indus; Nile; Tiber; Tigris; Yangtze Civilizations: Babylon; Kunming; Memphis; Mohenjo-Daro; Nineveh; Rome
Euphrates - Babylon, Indus - Mohenjo-Daro, Nile - Memphis, Tiber - Rome, Tigris - Nineveh, Yangtze - Kunming
Rome is on the Tiber. Two of these rivers are in Mesopotamia — Babylon and Nineveh sit on them.

Group the following Greek events according to the three major historical periods: Time Periods: Archaic Period; Classical Period; Hellenistic Period Events: Battle of the Hydaspes; Battle of Marathon; Battle of Salamis; Draconian reforms; First Macedonian War; First Punic War; Peloponnesian War
Archaic - Draconian reforms; Classical - Battle of Marathon, Battle of Salamis, Peloponnesian War; Hellenistic - First Macedonian War, Battle of the Hydaspes, First Punic War
Archaic comes first, then Classical (Marathon, Salamis), then Hellenistic — after Alexander.

Identify the city and state where, on February 14, 2018, 17 high school students were killed in a mass shooting. Then name the person who has become an outspoken national leader of the #NeverAgain movement to “fight our nation’s gun violence epidemic.”
A high school in south Florida, February 2018. The student leader's surname is one syllable.
On February 14, 2018, 17 high school students were killed in a mass shooting in this city and state, and this survivor became an outspoken national leader of the #NeverAgain movement.

Identify the following Revolutionary War battles: a) the battle in New York where British general John Burgoyne surrendered to American General Horatio Gates; b) the battle in Massachusetts where the order “Don’t fire until you see the whites of their eyes” was given; c) the battle in Virginia where British General Charles Cornwallis surrendered while a band played “The World Turned Upside Down.”
a) Saratoga; b) Bunker Hill; c) Yorktown
Saratoga was the turning point, Bunker Hill was the famous order to hold fire, Yorktown ended it.
List the currencies used in each of the following countries: Singapore, India, Mexico, France, and Russia.
Singapore = dollar; India = rupee; Mexico = peso; France = euro; Russia = ruble
Two of these five use a currency you would also spend in Spain or in the US.

Match each revolutionary invention to the current-day country where it originated: Inventions: camera; compass; nails; petroleum; printing press; steam engine Countries: China; Egypt; England; France; Germany; United States
camera - France, compass - China, nails - Egypt, petroleum - United States, printing press - Germany, steam engine - England
Gutenberg's press was German. Watt's engine was British. Gunpowder and the compass came from the same country.

Name these early explorers of the New World: a) the French explorer who founded Quebec and was governor of New France from 1633 to 1635; b) the English navigator who circumnavigated the globe, explored the west coast of North America, and commanded at the defeat of the Spanish Armada; c) the Spanish explorer who discovered the Mississippi River.
a) (Samuel de) Champlain; b) (Francis) Drake; c) (Hernando) De Soto
Quebec's founder gave his name to a lake. The English navigator beat the Armada. The Spaniard reached the Mississippi.
Name and describe Newton’s Three Laws of Motion

Newton’s First Law of Motion states that objects in motion remain in motion unless acted upon by an outside force; objects at rest stay at rest unless acted upon by an outside force. For example, if a ball is sitting on the floor, it will stay on the floor until someone kicks it. Newton’s Second Law of Motion states that the acceleration of an object is equal to the net force acting on it divided by an object’s mass. For example, when you throw a ball, the harder you throw, the more the ball accelerates. Newton’s Third Law of Motion states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Inertia, then F = ma, then action and reaction.
Identify the scientific instruments based on the following descriptions: a) it measures the specific gravity of liquids; b) it measures temperature; c) it measures air pressure.
a) hydrometer; b) thermometer; c) barometer
Hydro- means water, thermo- means heat, baro- means weight or pressure.
List the ten systems of the human body.
Cardiovascular, Digestive, Endocrine, Muscular, Nervous, Reproductive, Respiratory, Skeletal, Lymphatic, Urinary
Start with the ones you can point to: bones, muscles, heart, lungs, stomach. Then the control systems.
Identify the chemical element that: a) has the highest melting point, at 3,417 degrees Celsius; b) is the only metal that occurs naturally in a liquid state; c) is alloyed with tin to make bronze
Mercury is liquid at room temperature. Bronze is copper plus tin. The high-melting one is used in light bulb filaments.
List the seven taxonomy levels from largest to smallest: Class, Family, Genus, Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Species.
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
“King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.” Seven words, seven levels, largest first.
Explain the meaning of the slang words used in the following sentences: He had an ugly “mug”; She was wearing some very stylish “threads”; That game was a complete “rip-off.”
mug = face; threads = clothes; rip off = steal
Old slang: your mug is on your head, your threads are on your body.
List the following words in alphabetical order: Report, Academic, Presentation, Diagram, Pencil, Average, Scholastic, Drawing, Chart, Pen.
Academic, Average, Chart, Diagram, Drawing, Pen, Pencil, Presentation, Report, Scholastic
Alphabetical means letter by letter — so “pen” comes before “pencil,” not after.
State the meaning of the following abbreviations: a) T.B.A.; b) A.S.A.P.; c) P.O. Box; d) etc. (pronounce E-T-C.)
a) to be announced; b) as soon as possible; c) post office (box); d) etcetera
Three are ordinary phrases spelled out. The last is Latin, and it means “and the rest.”

State the title of the following Charles Dickens novels by their opening lines: a) “Marley was dead to begin with…” b) “It was the best of times, it was the worse of times…” c) “Whether I shall turn out to be the hero of my own life…” d) “My father’s family name being Pirrip…”
a) A Christmas Carol; b) A Tale of Two Cities; c) David Copperfield; d) Great Expectations
Marley is Scrooge's partner. “Best of times, worst of times” opens the French Revolution novel. Pirrip is Pip.

Define and identify the objective complements in the following sentences then state whether they are nouns or adjectives: a) “The man down the lane calls his farm Alfalfa.”; b) “The sergeant appointed the new recruit as leader of the group.”; c) “Diligent practice can make one a skilled person.”; d) “Many people named Lincoln the best president.” e) “Your irritableness makes everyone moody.”
a)alfalfa = noun; b) leader = noun; c) person = noun; d) president = noun; e) moody = adjective
An objective complement renames or describes the direct object. Four of these five are nouns.

Match each of the following poets with his/her published titles: Poets: Maya Angelou; Lewis Carroll; E.E. Cummings; Emily Dickinson; Robert Frost; Walt Whitman Titles: “All in green went my love riding”; “‘Hope’ is the Thing with Feathers”; “I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings”; “Jabberwocky”; “Nothing Gold Can Stay”; “O Captain! My Captain!”

Angelou - I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings; Carroll - Jabberwocky; Cummings - All in green went my love riding; Dickinson - ‘Hope’ is the Thing with Feathers; Frost - Nothing Gold Can Stay; Whitman - O Captain! My Captain!
Angelou's title is her own memoir. “Jabberwocky” is nonsense verse. Whitman wrote for Lincoln.

Determine if the following sentences require “it’s” or “its” in the blank: a. “____ easy to spot a comfortable T-shirt.” b. “The sock was missing ____ partner.” c. “This house is more expensive than ____ neighbors.” d. “Thanks for telling me that ____ raining outside.” e. “That yogurt is past ____ expiration date.”
a. it’s, b. its, c. its, d. it’s, e. its
“It's” always unpacks to “it is.” Try that in each blank and see which ones still make sense.

Determine if the following sentences require a hyphen; if so, indicate where the hyphen should be. a. “Henry prized his finely tuned Swiss watch.” b. “Jessica found a local, family owned restaurant.” c. “Forty four first graders went on the field trip.” d. “Our dog is four years old now.” e. “The new building featured state of the art design.”
a. No hyphen required, b. family-owned, c. Forty-four, d. No hyphen required, e. state-of-the-art
Hyphenate a compound only when the words act as one adjective before a noun. “Four years old” comes after.

Match each fictional character with his/her corresponding book title. Character: Aramis; Atticus Finch; Elizabeth Bennett; Gandalf; Napoleon; Scarlett O’Hara Book: Animal Farm; Gone with the Wind; The Lord of the Rings; Pride and Prejudice; The Three Musketeers; To Kill a Mockingbird
Aramis-Three Musketeers; Atticus Finch-To Kill a Mockingbird; Elizabeth Bennett- Pride and Prejudice; Gandalf-The Lord of the Rings; Napoleon-Animal Farm; Scarlett O’Hara- Gone with the Wind
Napoleon is a pig. Aramis is one of the three. Elizabeth Bennett is Austen's heroine.

Supply the animal missing from each of the following fable titles: Fables: “The Ant and the _________”; “The Boy Who Cried _________”; “The Lion and the _________”; “The Scorpion and the _________”; “The Tortoise and the _________”; “The Wolf in _________’s Clothing” Animals: Fish; Frog; Grasshopper; Hare; Mouse; Raven; Sheep; Wolf
The Ant and the Grasshopper; The Boy Who Cried Wolf; The Lion and the Mouse; The Scorpion and the Frog; The Tortoise and the Hare; The Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing
The ant worked all summer; someone else fiddled. The tortoise raced someone fast.

Match these works of literature with the time period of their settings: Works: A. A Night Divided, The Pigman B. Across Five Aprils, Rifles for Watie C. Chains, Spy D. Milkweed, The Book Thief E. Raven Queen, The Devil and His Boy F. The Matchlock Gun, The Witch of Blackbird Pond G. War Horse, Hattie Big Sky Setting: The Renaissance; Colonial America; The American Revolution; The American Civil War; World War I; World War II; the 1960s
A. the 1960s, B. American Civil War, C. American Revolution, D. World War II, E. the Renaissance, F. Colonial America, G. World War I
A Night Divided is about the Berlin Wall. Across Five Aprils is Civil War. Milkweed and The Book Thief are both Holocaust.

Match each literary work with the language in which it was first published: Works: A. Don Quixote B. Faust C. Les Misérables D. Pride and Prejudice E. The Divine Comedy F. The House of the Dead G. The Count of Monte Cristo Languages: English; French; German; Italian; Russian; Spanish

A. Don Quixote - Spanish, B. Faust - German, C. Les Misérables - French, D. Pride and Prejudice - English, E. The Divine Comedy - Italian, F. The House of the Dead - Russian, G. The Count of Monte Cristo - French
Cervantes wrote in Spanish, Goethe in German, Dante in Italian, Dostoevsky in Russian. Two are French.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Latin root cred: a. believable; reliable b. difficult to believe; extraordinary c. to undermine belief in someone or something d. a person who loans money with the expectation he or she will be paid back e. expressive of disbelief; skeptical f. dedicated to a religious purpose
a. credible, b. incredible, c. discredit, d. creditor, e. incredulous, f. sacred
Cred means believe. Add in-, dis-, -or, -ulous and see what you get.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Latin roots ben/bene: a. an advantage, profit, or gain b. a person who gives money to help or support a person or cause c. a person who receives money from someone else d. not harmful or malignant e. a blessing at the end of a religious service
a. benefit, b. benefactor, c. beneficiary, d. benign [do not accept beneficial], e. benediction
Bene means good or well. A -factor does it; a -ficiary receives it.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Latin root spect: a. someone who watches an event b. a public event or show; something that draws attention c. to view with doubt or suspicion d. a ghost or apparition e. a unique way of seeing or viewing events f. to consider or to look at something closely
a. spectator, b. spectacle, c. suspect, d. specter, e. perspective, f. inspect
Spect means look or watch. Add -ator, -acle, sus-, per-, in-.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Latin root ped: a. someone who travels on foot b. where your feet go on a bicycle c. an obstacle or something that blocks action or prevents progress d. a journey or voyage, usually for scientific purposes e. a device that measures your steps f. a cosmetic treatment of the feet and nails
a. pedestrian, b. pedal(s), c. impediment, d. expedition, e. pedometer, f. pedicure
Ped means foot. One of these is a Latin ped, and one on the list is about walking, not feet.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Latin root ject: a. to refuse, disagree with, or find unacceptable b. the path of something in motion c. a supposition or guess not based in fact d. something thrown or launched e. not influenced by emotions or personal prejudices f. to insert a comment into a conversation
a. reject [accept object], b. trajectory, c. conjecture, d. projectile [do not accept jet], e. objective [accept objectivity], f. interject [accept interjection]
Ject means throw. Re- throws back, tra- throws across, pro- throws forward, inter- throws between.

Supply the missing word in each saying: a. “All that ____ is not gold.” b. “Good things come to those who ____.” c. “Birds of a ____ flock together.” d. “____ killed the cat.” e. “Don’t add insult to ____.” f. “Don’t put all your ____ in one basket.”
a. glitters, b. wait, c. feather, d. curiosity, e. injury, f. eggs
Old sayings. (a) is about gold that isn't. (d) is about a curious cat.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Greek root chron: a. a list of events organized in order of occurrence b. something not belonging to a given time c. persisting for a long time or constantly recurring d. to align according to timing; to occur simultaneously e. a record of historical events that happen over time f. a device that measures the passing of time
a. chronology, b. anachronism [accept anachronistic], c. chronic, d. synchronize [accept synchronous], e. chronicle, f. chronometer
Chron means time. -ology is a study, -ic means lasting, syn- means together.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Greek root pan: a. a large gland in vertebrates b. a view in all directions c. a wild, uncontrollable uproar d. all the gods of a people or religion e. to express meaning through gestures f. something that spreads all over a country or the world
a. pancreas, b. panorama [accept panoramic], c. pandemonium, d. pantheon, e. pantomime, f. pandemic
Pan means all. A view in all directions; a disease over all the world; all the gods.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Greek root ant: a. a word having an opposite meaning b. a literary character who provides conflict c. given to undo harm or damage d. not wanting the company of others e. referring to the South Pole f. a strong feeling of dislike
a. antonym, b. antagonist, c. antidote, d. antisocial, e. antarctic [accept Antarctica], f. antipathy
Ant means against or opposite. An antonym is against the meaning; an antidote is against the poison.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Greek root demo: a. rule of or by the people b. one who supports rule by the people c. science that studies population statistics d. commonly found among a place or people e. a contagious disease that affects many people f. a state when people are noisy or hard to control
a. democracy, b. democrat, c. demography [accept demographics], d. endemic, e. epidemic, f. pandemonium
Demo means people. Rule by people; the study of people; a disease among people.

Supply the word described that incorporates the Greek root gram: a. a drawing that shows how something works b. a branch of linguistics dealing with sentence structure c. a word formed from another word by rearranging its letters d. a three-dimensional image made with lasers e. a listing of the order of events f. a unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a gram
a. diagram, b. grammar, c. anagram, d. hologram, e. program, f. milligram
Gram means something written or drawn. A drawing, a rearranged word, a laser image, a list of events.

Say and correct all incorrect words in the following sentence: We are learning state capitols, and we would like to visit some fo them when we have enough capitol. In the meantime, I will set here and study.
state capitals; enough capital, sit here
A capitol is the building; a capital is the city or the money. And “set” takes an object.

Supply the following words that derive from the Persian language. A correct list will be in alphabetical order and the first letter is given. a. a hired or professional killer (a____) b. an alloy of copper, tin, and other metals (b____) c. meat or other foods cooked on a skewer (k____) d. influencing events by calling on mysterious or supernatural forces (m____) e. a perfect place (p____) f. a percussion instrument with a wood frame and pairs of metal jingles (t____)
a. assassin, b. bronze, c. kebab [accept shish kebab], d. magic, e. paradise, f. tambourine
All Persian, all alphabetical: a-, b-, k-, m-, p-, t-. The last one is a tambourine's cousin.

Supply the following words that derive from the Persian language. A correct list will be in alphabetical order and the first letter is given. a. shades of pale or light brown (b____) b. a group of travelers journeying together (c____) c. a sour-tasting, yellow citrus fruit (l____) d. loose-fitting garments worn mostly for sleeping (p____) e. a bright red color (s____) f. the largest of the cat species with reddish-orange fur (t____)
a. beige, b. caravan, c. lemon, d. pajama, e. scarlet, f. tiger
All Persian, all alphabetical: b-, c-, l-, p-, s-, t-. The last is the biggest cat.

Supply the following words that derive from the Arabic language. A correct list will be in alphabetical order and the first letter is given. a. study of mathematical symbols and how to manipulate them (a____) b. a small, yellowish-orange fruit similar to a peach (a____) c. the tallest land animals in the world (g____) d. a wind that changes direction seasonally (m____) e. an overland journey, usually to view wildlife (s____) f. the highest point in a trajectory (z____)
a. algebra, b. apricot, c. giraffe, d. monsoon, e. safari, f. zenith
All Arabic, all alphabetical: a-, a-, g-, m-, s-, z-. The first is a branch of math.

Supply the following words that derive from the Old Norse language. A correct list will be in alphabetical order and the first letter is given. a. uncomfortable, abnormal, or ungainly (a____) b. a stupid or careless mistake (b____) c. to supply with items necessary for a particular purpose (e____) d. to sparkle with a bright, shimmering, reflected light (g____) e. strongly made or capable of withstanding rough handling (r____) f. to kill people or animals, typically in large numbers (s____)
a. awkward, b. blunder, c. equip, d. glitter, e. rugged, f. slaughter
All Old Norse, all alphabetical: a-, b-, e-, g-, r-, s-. Viking words, mostly rough ones.

Supply the following words that derive from the Scots language. A correct list will be in alphabetical order and the first letter is given. a. something demanded in return for not revealing injurious information (b____) b. a group of close-knit and/or interrelated families (c____) c. a quality that makes people or things seem appealing or special (g____) d. a checkered or tartan twilled cloth or pattern (p____) e. a horse of a small breed (p____) f. a sudden attack on an enemy by armed forces in warfare (r____)
a. blackmail, b. clan, c. glamour [glamorous], d. plaid, e. pony, f. raid
All Scots, all alphabetical: b-, c-, g-, p-, p-, r-. Two start with p and one is a fabric.
Explain the meaning of the following acronyms: PIN, NASA, WHO, and NATO.

acronym = a word or name formed as an abbreviation from the initial components in a phrase or a word. PIN = personal identification number. NASA = National Aeronautic Space Administration. WHO = World Health Organization. NATO = North Atlantic Treaty Organization
An acronym is pronounced as a word. Spell out what each set of letters stands for.

Match the following literary terms to their correct definitions: Terms: plot, suspense, dilemma, conflict, internal conflict Definitions: A problem or choice; Excitement for the outcome; Occurring within a character’s mind; Events making up a story; A challenge that characters need to solve; A conflicting situation for a character to choose between.

plot = events making up a story; suspense = excitement for the outcome; dilemma = a conflicting situation for a character to choose between; conflict = a challenge that characters need to solve; internal conflict = occurring within a character’s mind
Plot is what happens. Conflict is the problem. A dilemma is a choice between two bad options.
Name the part of the body referenced by each adjective: a. cardiac b. gastric c. lingual d. ocular e. pulmonary f. renal
a. heart, b. stomach, c. tongue, d. eyes, e. lungs, f. kidneys
Cardiac, gastric, lingual, ocular, pulmonary, renal — heart, stomach, tongue, eye, lung, kidney, but in which order?
Match each word with the country whose language it derives from: Words: bangle; boondocks; emoji; mammoth; slalom; yogurt; zombie Countries: Denmark; Haiti; India; Japan; Philippines; Russia; Turkey
bangle - India, boondocks - Philippines, emoji - Japan, mammoth - Russia, slalom - Denmark; yogurt - Turkey, zombie - Haiti
Emoji is obviously Japanese. Zombie came through voodoo. Slalom is a ski term from Scandinavia.

Match each example with its figurative language device used: Examples: “Every cloud has a silver lining.” “Foolish wisdom” “Your suitcase weighs a ton.” “The buzzing bee flew away.” ‘The flowers danced in the gentle breeze.” Devices: Hyperbole; Idiom; Onomatopoeia; Oxymoron, Personification
a - idiom, b - oxymoron, c - hyperbole, d - onomatopoeia, e - personification
“Silver lining” is a saying, not a literal one. “Foolish wisdom” contradicts itself. “Weighs a ton” exaggerates.
Jane, Jeff, Joe, and Jean each have a pet. Determine who has a dog, a cat, a bird, and a fish based on these facts: Jeff’s pet can’t fly Joe’s pet has hair, as does Jean’s Jean’s pet doesn’t bark
Only one pet flies, so that settles Jeff and Jane. Hair rules out the bird and the fish.
Calculate the number of distinct configurations that will result if Pedro has three cubes and he glues one face of each squarely to the face of another.
Face to face, the three cubes make a straight line or a bent one. That's it.
Pedro glues one face of each of three cubes squarely to the face of another, producing this many distinct configurations.
Arrange the digits 8, 2, 3, 5, 9 to: a) make the largest number possible; b) state the place value of the digit 8 in that number; c) state whether the number is divisible by 2, 3, 4, and 5.
a) 98,532; b) thousands; c) divisible by 2, 3 and 4, but not 5
Largest number means biggest digit first. Then check the last digit for 5, and the last two for 4.
Determine which of the following figures would not be changed in orientation by a one-quarter (90 degree) rotation: a square; a regular hexagon; an equilateral triangle; a circle; a right trapezoid.
After a quarter turn, which of these looks exactly the same? One has infinite symmetry; one has four-fold.
Of a square, a regular hexagon, an equilateral triangle, a circle, and a right trapezoid, these two are not changed in orientation by a one-quarter (90 degree) rotation.
Arrange all five people by height in descending order if: John is taller than Jason. Rebecca is taller than Jason. Sara is taller than John. Beverly is shorter than Rebecca and taller than Sara.
Start from the tallest clue: Beverly is under Rebecca but over Sara, and Sara is over John.

Mark, Mike, Mary, and Max each weigh different amounts. Determine who weighs 80 pounds, 90 pounds, 100 pounds, and 110 pounds based on these facts: Mark weighs more than Mike Max weighs less than Mary Max weighs 20 pounds more than Mike Mary weighs more than Mark
Mark-90 pounds, Mike-80 pounds, Mary-110 pounds, Max-100 pounds
Max is 20 more than Mike, and Mary is the heaviest. Work from those two facts.
Name the type of angle that has each of the given measures: A) eighty five degrees, B) one hundred eighty degrees, C) ninety-two degrees, D) twelve degrees
a. acute, b. straight, c. obtuse, d. acute
Under 90 is acute, exactly 90 is right, over 90 is obtuse, exactly 180 is straight.
Give the sum of the measures of all the interior angles in a) a rhombus b) a hexagon, c) an octagon, d) a scalene triangle.
a. 360 degrees, b. 720 degrees, c. 1080 degrees, d. 180 degrees
Every extra side adds 180 degrees. A four-sided figure has 360.

Identify which of the following polyhedra (paw-lee-hee-druh) have the same number of faces: square pyramid; pentagonal pyramid; hexagonal prism; triangular pyramid; octagonal pyramid; rectangular prism
Count faces: a pyramid has its base plus one face per side. A prism has two bases plus the sides.
Of a square pyramid, pentagonal pyramid, hexagonal prism, triangular pyramid, octagonal pyramid, and rectangular prism, these two have the same number of faces.
State whether each of the following numbers is divisible by 3 and 5, but not 2: a) 990; b) 1125; c) 975; d) 995; e) 1025.
a) no; b) yes; c) yes; d) no; e) no
Divisible by 5 means it ends in 0 or 5. “Not by 2” means it must be odd — so anything ending in 0 is out.
Determine which quadrant the line that passes through (0,4) and (1,3) will NOT go through?
The line drops one for every step right, so its slope is negative and it crosses at 4. Sketch it.
The line passing through (0,4) and (1,3) never enters this quadrant.
Find the slope and y-intercept of each equation: a) 6x − 2y = 8; b) 7x = 10 − y; c) −6x + 3y = 15; d) y = 4x − 6.
a) slope 3, y-intercept −4; b) slope −7, y-intercept 10; c) slope 2, y-intercept 5; d) slope 4, y-intercept −6
Rearrange each into y = mx + b. The number in front of x is the slope; the leftover is the intercept.

Calculate the amount of money in the account at the end of 6 months if a savings account earns 1 percent interest per month on the sum of the initial amount deposited plus any accumulated interest. The savings account was opened with an initial deposit of $1,000 and no other deposits or withdrawals were made.
One percent a month for six months is not six percent — the interest earns interest.
A savings account opened with $1,000 earns 1 percent interest a month on the deposit plus accumulated interest, with no other deposits or withdrawals, leaving this balance after 6 months.
Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in: a) a hexagon; b) an octagon; c) a nonagon; d) a decagon; e) a dodecagon
a. 9 diagonals, b. 20 diagonals, c. 27 diagonals, d. 35 diagonals, e. 54 diagonals
Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.
Which of the following pairs of angles are always congruent? A) supplementary B) vertical C) corresponding D) alternate exterior E) complementary
Which pair sits directly across from each other where two lines cross?
Of supplementary, vertical, corresponding, alternate exterior, and complementary angles, this pair is always congruent.
Calculate the sum of the 100 numbers in this series: 1 + - 2 + 3 + - 4 + 5 + - 6 + …+ 99 + - 100
Pair them up: 1 − 2 is −1, 3 − 4 is −1. How many pairs are there?
This is the sum of the 100 numbers in the series 1 + −2 + 3 + −4 + 5 + −6 + … + 99 + −100.

Determine the probability that a card selected at random from a deck of 52 cards is a) the suit of hearts; b) a face card; c) the number ten; d) a suit of club or spade. State your answer as a reduced fraction.
a) ¼ (one-fourth); b) 3/13 (three-thirteenths); c) 1/13 (one-thirteenth); d) ½ (one-half)
52 cards, 13 hearts, 12 face cards, 4 tens, 26 black. Reduce each fraction.

The lunch-ordering app for Savage Pizza asks you to choose two distinct meats from among pepperoni, Canadian bacon and sausage; or to choose two distinct vegetables from among mushrooms, onions, green peppers and black olives; or to choose one meat and one vegetable from among the same choices. Calculate how many different pizza combinations are possible using the lunch-ordering app.
Three separate cases: two meats, two vegetables, or one of each. Add them up.

Savage Pizza’s lunch app lets you pick two distinct meats from pepperoni, Canadian bacon and sausage; or two distinct vegetables from mushrooms, onions, green peppers and black olives; or one meat and one vegetable — this many combinations are possible.

On Saturday, three different baseball games are televised at noon and four different games are televised at 8 p.m. On Sunday, five different games are televised at noon. If Armando watches one Saturday game at noon and another at 8 p.m. and one game at noon on Sunday, calculate how many different combinations of games can he watch.
Three different games are televised Saturday at noon and four at 8 p.m., and five different games Sunday at noon; Armando watches one from each group, giving this many combinations.

In a new Scrabble theme, a sequence of letters is considered a word if the first and last letters are consonants and every letter in between is a vowel. In this game, how many four-letter words can be formed using each of the letters D, R, A, G, O, N, T, U, and B no more than once?
First and last must be consonants, middle two vowels. Count the consonants and vowels available, then multiply.

In a Scrabble theme where a word begins and ends with a consonant and has only vowels in between, this many four-letter words can be built from D, R, A, G, O, N, T, U, and B, using each no more than once.

Several students were trying out for a class play. When asked which roles they were willing to play, 12 of them were willing to play the knight, 15 were willing to play the troll, and 6 were willing to play the wizard. Of these students, 8 were willing to play either the knight or the troll, 5 were willing to play the knight or the wizard, and 4 were willing to play the troll or the wizard. Exactly 3 of these students were willing to play any of the roles. How many students were willing to play only the wizard and no other role?
Draw a three-circle Venn diagram and fill in the middle first.

Trying out for a class play: 12 students were willing to play the knight, 15 the troll, 6 the wizard, 8 the knight or troll, 5 the knight or wizard, 4 the troll or wizard, and exactly 3 any role — this many were willing to play only the wizard.

Match the National Park with the state in which it is located: National Parks: Zion; Joshua Tree; Congaree; Everglades; Rocky Mountains; Olympic; Denali; Crater Lake States: Alaska; California; Colorado; Florida; Oregon; South Carolina; Utah; Washington
Zion - Utah, Joshua Tree - California, Congaree - South Carolina, Everglades - Florida, Rocky Mountains - Colorado, Olympic - Washington, Denali - Alaska, Crater Lake - Oregon
Zion is red rock; Congaree is a swamp forest; Denali is the highest peak.

Match each American landmark with the state in which it is located: Landmarks: Carlsbad Cavern; Gateway Arch; Hoover Dam; Independence Hall; Monticello; Mount Rushmore; Niagara Falls; The Alamo States: Missouri; Nevada; New Mexico; New York; Pennsylvania; South Dakota; Texas; Virginia

Carlsbad Cavern - New Mexico, Gateway Arch - Missouri, Hoover Dam - Nevada, Independence Hall - Pennsylvania, Monticello - Virginia, Mount Rushmore - South Dakota, Niagara Falls - New York, The Alamo - Texas
Monticello was Jefferson's home. The Alamo is in San Antonio. Carlsbad is a cave.

Match each National Cemetery with the state in which it is located: Cemeteries: Yorktown; Vicksburg; Shiloh; Gettysburg; Antietam; Andersonville States: Georgia; Maryland; Mississippi; Pennsylvania; Tennessee; Virginia
Andersonville - Georgia, Antietam - Maryland, Gettysburg - Pennsylvania, Shiloh - Tennessee, Vicksburg - Mississippi, Yorktown - Virginia
All six are Civil War battlefields. Gettysburg and Antietam were fought in the North.

Match each National Military Park with the state in which it is located: Parks: Chickamauga; Fredericksburg; Gettysburg; Guilford Courthouse; Kings Mountain; Shiloh; Vicksburg States: Georgia; Mississippi; North Carolina; Pennsylvania; South Carolina; Tennessee; Virginia
Chickamauga - Georgia; Fredericksburg - Virginia; Gettysburg - Pennsylvania; Guilford Courthouse - North Carolina; Kings Mountain - South Carolina; Shiloh - Tennessee; Vicksburg - Mississippi
Guilford Courthouse and Kings Mountain are Revolutionary War, in the Carolinas. The rest are Civil War.

Match each presidential home with the state in which it is located: Homes: Franklin Pierce Homestead; Lincoln Home; Mount Vernon (George Washington); Peacefield (John Adams); Sagamore Hill (Theodore Roosevelt); The Hermitage (Andrew Jackson) States: Illinois; Massachusetts; New Hampshire; New York; Tennessee; Virginia
Pierce - New Hampshire, Lincoln - Illinois, Washington - Virginia, Adams - Massachusetts, Roosevelt - New York, Jackson - Tennessee
Mount Vernon is on the Potomac. The Hermitage is near Nashville. Sagamore Hill is on Long Island.

Identify the US state where each landmark is located: a) Pike’s Peak; b) Adirondack (ad-er-on-dack) Mountains; c) Yosemite (yo-sehm-ih-tee) National Park; d) Stone Mountain; e) Cumberland Mountains; f) The Berkshires (berk-shy-ers)
a) Colorado; b) New York; c) California; d) Georgia; e) Tennessee; f) Massachusetts
Pike's Peak is in the Rockies. The Berkshires are in New England. Stone Mountain is near Atlanta.

Identify the Southeast Asian country where the United Nations said in 2018 that top generals should face trial for genocide. Then name the targeted ethnic minority group; it is described as one of the most persecuted groups on the planet.
Myanmar (also known as Burma), group = Rohingya (Ro-hing-guh) - a stateless Muslim minority group
The country was formerly called Burma. The minority group is Muslim and stateless.

In a race with five people, Alex finished ahead of Dustin, and the same number of people finished before Alex that finished after Dustin. Brandon finished before Casey and Alex finished after Peter. Who finished in third place?
Five racers, and the same number finished before Alex as after Dustin. That pins Alex and Dustin symmetrically.
In a five-person race Alex finished ahead of Dustin with as many people ahead of Alex as behind Dustin, Brandon finished before Casey, and Alex finished after Peter — this runner came in third.
State the SI (System International) prefix for each of the following: a) one hundredth; b) one thousandth; c) one thousand; d) one billionth; e) one millionth.
a) centi-; b) milli-; c) kilo-; d) nano-; e) micro-
Centi, milli, kilo, nano, micro — but which goes with which? Nano is the smallest.

Determine a) who sits in the front seat; b) who sits in the second seat, and c) who sits in the last seat if Parker, Nathan, Jessica, Alisha, and Eric are seated in the same row. The girls are not on either end. Eric is not next to a girl not at the back, and Nathan is not next to Eric.
a) Eric; b) Nathan; c) Parker
Girls can't be on the ends, so the two ends are boys. Then use the “not next to” clues.

At 10 a.m. a car dealer had 30 cars that were either blue or green. At 2 p.m. after selling 2 green cars and no blue cars, the dealer had 3 times as many green cars as blue cars. How many green cars did the dealer have at 10 a.m.?
After selling 2, greens equal three times blues, and the total is 28. Set it up as one equation.
At 10 a.m. a dealer had 30 cars, all blue or green; by 2 p.m., after selling 2 green cars and no blue ones, he had three times as many green as blue — so he started the day with this many green cars.
Match each of the following geometric figures with its number of sides: a. hexagon, b. heptagon, c. decagon, d. pentagon, e. octagon/ten, six, eight, seven, five
Hex is six, hept is seven, oct is eight, dec is ten, pent is five.

While drawing with his computer tablet, Gabriel changed the dimensions of a rectangle so that the new rectangle was ½ as tall and ¼ as wide as the original rectangle. What is the ratio of the area of the new rectangle to the area of the original rectangle? Express your answer as a common fraction.
Half the height times a quarter the width. Multiply the two fractions.
Gabriel redraws a rectangle ½ as tall and ¼ as wide as the original; as a common fraction, this is the ratio of the new area to the old.

A triangle has a base of 3 feet and a height of 6 feet. If its area is increased to 35 square feet by increasing the base and height by the same number of feet, what is the sum of the new base and height?
