Old area is 9. New area is 35. Write (3+x)(6+x)/2 = 35 and solve for x, then add the new base and height.

A triangle with a base of 3 feet and a height of 6 feet reaches an area of 35 square feet when the base and height each grow by the same number of feet, making this the sum of the new base and height.

If using a standard deck of 52 cards, what is the probability of retrieving each of the following?: ‘A queen of hearts’, ‘a black ace’, ‘a number four’, and ‘a red six’. Answer with its most reduced fraction.
a queen of hearts = 1/52, a black ace = 1/26, a number four = 1/13, a red six = 1/26
Out of 52: one specific card, two black aces, four fours, two red sixes. Reduce.

Determine the sitting order of three girls from left to right and the color of the uniforms they are wearing if three cheerleaders are sitting side by side and Ali is to the right of Jen and Lisa, the red uniform is to the left of Jen, and the green uniform is to the right of the blue uniform.
Lisa is in red, Jen is in blue, Ali is in green
Ali is right of both others, so Ali is on the right. Red is left of Jen, so Jen isn't in red.

Calculate how many hours in each of 3 practices a team must have in week five to average 6 (six) hours of practice each week for five weeks if a team practiced 2 times for 1-½ (one and a half) hours the 1st week; 3 times for 2-¼ (two and a fourth) hours the 2nd week; 2 times for 1-½ (one and a half) hours the 3rd week; and 4 times for 3 hours the 4th week.
Each of the team’s 3 practices in week 5 were 1-¾ (one and three quarters) hours long.
Five weeks at 6 hours is 30 hours total. Add up the first four weeks and split the rest three ways.

Calculate how far Martin walked if he walked half of the total distance in the morning, stopping at noon for lunch. After lunch, he walked one-third of the remaining distance and still had 6 miles to go.
Work backwards. The 6 miles left is two-thirds of the afternoon half.
Martin walked half the total distance before lunch, then one-third of what was left, and still had 6 miles to go — this is the whole distance in miles.

Match each term with the subject of its study: 1. Ecology 2. Paleontology, 3. Petrology, 4. Speleology, 5. Vulcanology A. study of ancient life, B. study of caves, C. study of how organisms interact with the environment, D. study of volcanoes, E. study of rocks and their formation
Ecology - C, Paleontology - A, Petrology - E, Speleology - B, Vulcanology - D
Speleo is caves, vulcano is volcanoes, petro is rock, paleo is ancient, eco is environment.

Match the following Supreme Court cases with their outcomes: a). Ruled that states could not deny legal counsel to defendants, b). Ruled that public school segregation was unconstitutional, c). Ruled that those in police custody must be made aware of their rights, d). Ruled that evidence collected by police during a search is only admissible with a warrant signed by a judge. 1. Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, 2. Gideon v. Wainwright, 3. Mapp v. Ohio, 4. Miranda v. Arizona
a. Gideon, b. Brown, c. Miranda, d. Mapp
Gideon got the lawyer, Brown got the schools, Miranda got the rights read, Mapp got the warrant.

Name each city of the ancient world: a. the Agora was its central meeting place b. its library was the largest in the world c. its “hanging gardens” were world famous d. connected by its system of roads e. its trade empire was destroyed after 146 BC f. contains holy sites to three major religions
a. Athens, b. Alexandria, c. Babylon, d. Rome, e. Carthage, f. Jerusalem
The Agora was Greek. The hanging gardens were Mesopotamian. All roads lead somewhere.
Explain the difference between simple interest and compound interest.

Simple interest is paid or received over a certain period and is a fixed percentage of the principal amount that was borrowed or lent. Compound interest accrues and is added to the accumulated interest of previous periods; it includes interest on interest
One kind is always a percentage of the original amount. The other earns interest on interest.
Identify the island territory that President Trump said he would like to purchase, and the country that governs the island.
The world's largest island, and it belongs to a small Scandinavian country.
State four of the rights guaranteed by the First Amendment of the US Constitution.
FOUR OF THE FOLLOWING: 1. Freedom of speech; 2. Freedom of press; 3. Freedom of religion; 4. Freedom of peaceable assembly; 5. Freedom of requesting (petitioning for) changes in the government.
Speech, press, religion, assembly, petition. Name any four.
Name the eight parts of speech.
Nouns, Pronouns, Verbs, Adjectives, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions, Interjections
Eight jobs a word can do: naming, standing in for a name, acting, describing, modifying, positioning, joining and exclaiming. The extras on the board are verb forms and a kind of adjective.
If canine means dog-like and feline means cat-like, to which animals do the following adjectives refer? A. Leonine B. Lupine C. Equine D. Ursine E. Porcine F. Avian G. Bovine H. Simian
a. Lion, b. Wolf, c. Horse, d. Bear, e. Pig, f. Bird, g. Cow, h. Monkey
Leo is lion, lupus is wolf, equus is horse, ursus is bear, porcus is pig, avis is bird, bos is cow, simia is ape.
Match each word built on the Latin root “sub” to its definition: 1. subcutaneous; 2. substitution; 3. subpar; 4. subconscious.
1. subcutaneous – under the skin; 2. substitution – to replace; 3. subpar – below an acceptable level; 4. subconscious – in your mind
Sub means under or below. Under the skin; below acceptable; below awareness; put one under another.
Match each word built on the Latin root “mal” to its definition: 1. malpractice; 2. malevolent; 3. maladaptive; 4. malfunction.
1. malpractice – a job was done badly; 2. malevolent – the act of being evil; 3. maladaptive – changing to a situation badly; 4. malfunction – does not work well
Mal means bad. Bad practice, bad will, badly adapted, bad function.
Match each word built on the Latin root “audi” to its definition: 1. audience; 2. audiologist; 3. audible; 4. audition.
1. audience – a crowd that listens to a performance; 2. audiologist – a person who studies how a person hears; 3. audible – able to be heard; 4. audition – a try-out where you are listened to
Audi means hear. Those who hear; one who studies hearing; able to be heard; a listening try-out.

Complete each of the following sentences with its appropriate homophone: Sally spoke with the school’s (principal/principle) after behaving improperly. Jason attempted to (complement/compliment) his opponent for a job well done. Daniel moved from Illinois to Arizona in order to escape the cold (weather/whether).
A principal is a person or the main thing; a principle is a rule. A compliment is praise.
Beginning with the first novel in the series, name J.K. Rowling’s seven installments of Harry Potter in chronological order.

Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone; Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets; Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban; Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire; Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix; Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince; Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
Stone, Chamber, Prisoner, Goblet, Order, Prince, Hallows.

Arrange these seven scrambled Harry Potter novels in the order of which they were created, beginning with the introductory novel: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix; Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets; Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows; Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone; Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince; Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban; Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.

Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone; Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets; Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban; Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire; Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix; Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince; Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
Stone, Chamber, Prisoner, Goblet, Order, Prince, Hallows.

Arrange the seven “Shadow Children” novels, by Margaret Haddix in the order of which they were created, beginning with the introductory novel: Among the Imposters; Among the Brave; Among the Free, Among the Hidden; Among the Barons; Among the Enemy and Among the Betrayed.
Among the Hidden; Among the Imposters; Among the Betrayed; Among the Barons; Among the Brave; Among the Enemy and Among the Free).
“Hidden” comes first — it introduces Luke. “Free” is the last word of the series.

Complete each of the following compound sentences with the most appropriate coordinating conjunction: Jake is an excellent trumpet player, (but/and) his piano skills are subpar. All of my friends were busy, (and/so) I had to see the movie by myself. We have never traveled to Texas, (or/nor) have we visited Utah. She decided against littering her trash, (for/and) it was the wrong thing to do. Sam likes to surf, (but/and) he is going surfing this weekend.
FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so. Match each to the relationship between the two clauses.

Complete each of the following sentences with its appropriate preposition: ‘after’, ‘along’, ‘across’, ‘above’ Stephanie was chosen as team captain because she gets _______ with all of her teammates. Mrs. Smith is a great coach who takes pride in looking _______ her student-athletes. The student received detention for throwing the football _______ the classroom. Jenna’s softball team won more games and finished _______ Emily’s softball team in the final season standings.
List eight types of punctuation marks.
ANY EIGHT OF THE FOLLOWING: apostrophe, braces, brackets, colon, comma, dash, exclamation mark/point, hyphen, parentheses, period, question mark, quotation marks, semicolon
Period, comma, question mark, exclamation, apostrophe, quotation marks, colon, semicolon — that's already eight.
Match each of the following dystopian novels with its appropriate author: Brave New World, Fahrenheit 451, The Hunger Games, The Giver/Suzanne Collins, Lois Lowry, Ray Bradbury, Aldous Huxley
Brave New World/Aldous Huxley; Fahrenheit 451/Ray Bradbury; The Hunger Games/Suzanne Collins; The Giver/Lois Lowry
Huxley wrote the one about a designed society. Bradbury's is the burning temperature of paper.
Define each of the following types of writing: memo, memoir, myth

memo = a brief note usually having to do with business; memoir = recollections of a famous person’s life, along with his/her reflections; myth = an explanation of elements in nature or the origin of traditions
One is a short business note. One is a life story told by the person who lived it. One explains nature.
Conjugate the verb “ring” in the present perfect tense.
I have rung, you have rung, he/she/it has rung, we have rung, you have rung, they have rung
Present perfect uses “have” or “has” plus the past participle. Ring, rang, rung.
Name the authors of the following works: Casey at the Bat; The Wonderful Wizard of Oz; Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm.
Casey at the Bat = (Lawrence) Thayer; The Wonderful Wizard of Oz = (L. Frank) Baum; Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm = (Kate Douglas) Wiggin
“Casey at the Bat” is a baseball poem. Oz was written by a man with initials.
Name the five steps to the writing process.
Pre-writing, drafting, revising, editing and publishing
Pre-writing, drafting, revising, editing, and one more that means sharing it.

Identify the two words from the following sentence which are onomatopoeic (ah-nah-maht-ah-pee-yik): “He tried to hum a favorite hymn, but the pattering of large raindrops on the roof broke his rhythm.”
Onomatopoeia means the word sounds like the thing. “Hymn” and “rhythm” are spelling traps, not sounds.
In “He tried to hum a favorite hymn, but the pattering of large raindrops on the roof broke his rhythm,” these two words are onomatopoeic.
Restate the following sentence and include any missing punctuation. “Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school she went to Starbucks.”
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school; she went to Starbucks.
Two complete sentences are jammed together. Join them with the mark that is stronger than a comma.
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school, she went to Starbucks.
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school: she went to Starbucks.
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee, before school she went to Starbucks.
This is “Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school she went to Starbucks,” restated with the punctuation it was missing.

Read “The Sea,” a poem by James Reeves, and identify three examples of figurative language: “The sea is a hungry dog, / Giant and grey. / He rolls on the beach all day. / With his clashing teeth and shaggy jaws, / Hour upon hour, he gnaws / The rumbling, tumbling stones, / And ‘Bones, bones, bones, bones!’ / The giant sea dog moans, / Licking his greasy paws.”

ANY THREE OF THE FOLLOWING: metaphor (“the sea is a hungry dog”); personification (“he rolls on the beach”, “the giant sea dog moans”); onomatopoeia (“clashing”, “rumbling, tumbling”); imagery (“hour upon hour, he gnaws”)
“The sea is a hungry dog” says it is, not “like.” And a dog that moans and gnaws is being given human traits.
List four of the five Romance languages spoken in the world today, and then explain why they are called Romance languages.
ANY FOUR OF THE FOLLOWING: French, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian (or Romanish) and Spanish. They are called Romance languages because they grew out of Latin, the language of ancient Rome.
They all grew out of one ancient language spoken in Rome. Four of the five are easy; the fifth is in Eastern Europe.
Identify what ion is found in the following substances: Acids; Bases; Salts; Water.
Acids = hydrogen ion; Bases = hydroxide ion; Salts = no ions; Water = hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions.
Acids donate H+. Bases give OH−. Water does a little of both. Salts are neutral.
Match each state with its correct capital: Idaho, Illinois, Iowa, Indiana/Des Moines, Springfield, Indianapolis, Boise
All four states start with I. Boise, Des Moines, Indianapolis, Springfield — one of them is the odd match.

Identify the following planets in our solar system; a) the 4th planet from the sun; b) the planet similar in size to Earth with a thick cover of clouds; c) the largest planet in our solar system; d) the planet that has rings.
a) Mars; b) Venus; c) Jupiter; d) Saturn
The red one; the cloudy one that's Earth's twin; the biggest one; the one with the famous rings.
State the temperature of boiling & freezing water on both the Fahrenheit (fair-uhn-heyet) and the Celsius (sell-see-us) scale.
Fahrenheit: 212° boiling, 32° freezing. Celsius: 100° boiling, 0° freezing
212 and 32 on one scale; 100 and 0 on the other.
Identify the member of our solar system whose definition was changed to ‘dwarf planet’ in 2006. Explain its former definition and position in the solar system.
Pluto; former definition = planet; position = ninth from the sun
It got demoted in 2006 and used to be counted ninth.
List the five US states that the Colorado River flows through or borders.
Two are named after the river's own region, and the river ends at the Mexican border. Think Grand Canyon.
List the five US state capitals that start with the letter “A” and their states.
Augusta, Maine; Annapolis, Maryland; Albany, New York; Austin, Texas; Atlanta, Georgia
Two are in New England, one is a Southern state capital named for a Georgia river, and the biggest of the five is in Texas.

Identify the following: a) the country that hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics; b) the city where the opening ceremonies were held; c) the date of the opening ceremonies; d) the last time the Olympics were held in that country.
a) China; b) Beijing; c) August 8, 2008 (8/8/08); d) never — it was the first time
The date was chosen because the digits repeat. And it was the country's first time hosting.
Define longitude and latitude, and identify what lies at 0 (zero) degrees longitude, and what lies at 0 (zero) degrees latitude.

longitude: distance on the earth’s surface measured east or west from the Prime Meridian at Greenwich, England; latitude - the distance on the earth’s surface north or south of the Equator; the Prime Meridian (Greenwich (grenn-itch), England) lies at (zero) degrees longitude; the Equator
Longitude lines run north-south and are measured from Greenwich. Latitude lines run east-west from the Equator.

State whether each of the following is thousands, millions, billions, or trillions of miles from the Earth: a) the average distance to the Earth’s moon; b) the average distance to the sun; c) the average distance to Mars.
a) thousands (about 240,000 miles); b) millions (about 93 million); c) millions (about 65 million)
The moon is about 240,000 miles away; the sun about 93 million. Mars is closer than the sun.
Define the following terms: a) carnivore; b) herbivore; c) omnivore.
a) an animal that eats flesh; b) an animal that only eats plants; c) an animal that eats both plants and flesh
Carn is flesh, herb is plant, omni is all.
List the US states that share a border with Mississippi.
Four states touch it. Two are named after rivers, and one is directly north.
List six of the seven US states that border Kentucky.
ANY SIX OF THE FOLLOWING: Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Ohio, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia
Seven touch Kentucky; name any six. The Ohio River forms most of the northern border.
Identify the capital city of each of the following Western States: Oregon; New Mexico; Texas; California; Idaho.
Oregon = Salem; New Mexico = Santa Fe; Texas = Austin; California = Sacramento; Idaho = Boise
Salem, Santa Fe, Austin, Sacramento, Boise — now pair them up.
List the five Great Lakes in the US from largest to smallest.
Superior is biggest, Ontario smallest. HOMES gives you the names but not the order.
List the four original New England colonies.
New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Massachusetts (accept Maine)
Four colonies: two small ones, one big one, and one named for a river. Maine was part of one of them.
List the US states that share a border with Ohio.
Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Pennsylvania, West Virginia
Five states touch Ohio. The river along the south is its own border.
Calculate how many comic books Tim has if he has three times as many comic books as Betsy. Betsy has two-thirds as many comic books as Curt, and Curt has 27 comic books.
Curt has 27, Betsy has two-thirds of that, Tim has three times Betsy's.
Tim has three times as many comic books as Betsy, Betsy has two-thirds as many as Curt, and Curt has 27, so Tim has this many.
State the term used to identify the offspring of a: bird; deer; seal; whale; rat; goat; kangaroo.
bird = fledgling (accept nestling); deer = fawn (accept yearling); seal = pup; whale = calf; rat = pup; goat = kid; kangaroo = joey
A young goat is a kid, a young deer is a fawn, a young kangaroo is a joey. Seals and whales borrow other words.
List six different forms of energy.
Any six of the following: 1. electrical; 2. mechanical; 3. light; 4. heat; 5. chemical; 6. nuclear; 7. sound
Electrical, mechanical, light, heat, chemical, nuclear, sound — name any six.
State and define the three categories that make up the food chain.
1. producer — uses the sun’s energy to produce food; 2. consumer — consumes food in the form of plants and other animals; 3. decomposer — breaks down organic matter into minerals plants can reuse
One makes food from sunlight, one eats, one breaks down what's left.
Identify and describe the three processes involved in the water cycle.

1. evaporation: the process of liquid turning into vapor; 2. condensation: water vapor cools and turns back into liquid droplets; 3. precipitation: the condensed molecules become so heavy that they fall
Water rises as vapor, gathers into clouds, then falls.
State whether each of the following is a reptile, mammal, amphibian, fish, or bird: condor, armadillo, perch, humpback whale.
condor = bird; armadillo = mammal; perch = fish; humpback whale = mammal
A condor flies, an armadillo has hair, a perch has gills, and a whale breathes air.
Classify each of the following animals as mammal, fish, amphibian, reptile or bird: a) frog; b) penguin; c) platypus; d) crocodile; e) whale
a)frog = amphibian; b) penguin = bird; c) platypus = mammal; d) crocodile = reptile; e) whale = mammal
Frogs start life in water; penguins have feathers; a platypus lays eggs but still has fur.

Identify the following as transparent, translucent, or opaque: a) Any material that scatters light as it passes through; b) Any material that transmits light; c) Any material that reflects or absorbs all light that strikes it.
a) translucent; b) transparent; c) opaque
Transparent lets light straight through; translucent scatters it; opaque blocks it.

State the following layers of atmosphere in order from the highest to altitude to the lowest altitude: stratosphere (stra-toh-sfeer), ionosphere (eye-on-oh-sfeer), (Aurora), troposphere (troh-poh-sfeer), mesosphere (meh-zoh-sfeer).
MUST BE IN THIS ORDER: ionosphere (Aurora), mesosphere, stratosphere, troposphere
Highest first: ionosphere, then mesosphere, then stratosphere, then the one we live in.
List four factors that help determine climate.
ANY FOUR OF THE FOLLOWING: temperature, moisture, altitude, radiant energy, latitude
Temperature, moisture, altitude, radiant energy, latitude — name any four.

Arrange the following to give the correct sequence for the flow of blood through the heart: 1. lungs; 2. aorta; 3. right atrium; 4. left atrium; 5. right ventricle; 6. left ventricle; 7. pulmonary veins; 8. pulmonary artery
3. right atrium; 5. right ventricle; 8. pulmonary artery; 1. Lungs; 7 pulmonary veins; 4. left atrium; 6. left ventricle; 2. aorta
Blood comes in on the right side, goes to the lungs, comes back to the left side, then out the aorta.

Identify the following objects as being either a lever or an incline plane: screw; wheelbarrow; wheelchair ramp; nutcracker. Say both the name of the object and the type of the simple machine in your answer.
screw = incline plane; wheelbarrow = lever; wheelchair ramp = incline plane; nutcracker = lever
A screw is a ramp wrapped around a cylinder. A wheelbarrow and a nutcracker both pivot.

State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in each of the following four neutral atoms: a) silicon which has an atomic number of 14 and an atomic mass of 28; b) zinc which has 30 electrons and an atomic mass of 65; c) neon which is a Noble gas and has an atomic mass of 20; d) oxygen which has an atomic number of 8 and an atomic mass of 17.
a) 14 protons, 14 electrons, 14 neutrons; b) 30 protons, 30 electrons, 35 neutrons; c) 10 protons, 10 electrons, 10 neutrons; d) 8 protons, 8 electrons, 9 neutrons
In a neutral atom, protons equal electrons and equal the atomic number. Neutrons are mass minus protons.
List five types of information a person can receive from each square found on the Periodic Table of Elements.

ANY FIVE OF THE FOLLOWING: number of protons, number of electrons, # of neutrons, atomic number, atomic mass, symbol, element name, number of electrons in each orbit, valence, kind of atom (i.e. metal vs. non-metal
Each square shows the symbol, the name, the atomic number and the atomic mass — and from those you can work out more.
Identify the following rocks as igneous (ig-nee-us), sedimentary, or metamorphic: a) granite; b) shale; c) slate; d) quartzite.
a) igneous; b)sedimentary, c) metamorphic; d) metamorphic
Granite cools from magma. Shale is packed mud. Slate and quartzite are both squeezed versions of something else.
Explain the difference between a territory and a state in the United States.

A territory is a region or district that is not admitted to the Union as a state, is under more Federal control, & has its own legislative and governing officials. A state must have a written constitution, at least 60,000 citizens, and be organized under one government. Federal control is less in a state than in a territory.
One is admitted to the Union and writes its own constitution; the other answers more to the federal government.
List the following colors of light in order of decreasing frequency: 1. Green; 2. Red; 3. Violet; 4. Orange; 5. Blue; 6. Yellow
3. violet; 5. blue; 1. green; 6. yellow; 4. orange; 2. red
ROYGBIV, backwards. Violet has the highest frequency.
Match the following monetary systems and the country they are associated with: MONETARY SYSTEM = Euro, dollar, rupee, yen, peso; COUNTRIES = Mexico, Japan, US, Germany, India
Euro = Germany; dollar = US; rupee = India; yen =Japan; peso = Mexico
Germany uses the shared European currency. India's is the rupee, Japan's the yen, Mexico's the peso.
State the following about the United Nations: a) The primary objective; b) The war after which the United Nations was founded; c) The city where its headquarters is located.
a) To promote world peace; b)World War II; c) New York City
It was founded in 1945, right after a war, and its headquarters is on the East River.
Identify the “Five Civilized Tribes” of Native Americans who were forced to resettle in Oklahoma in the 1830s.
Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Creek, Seminole — the Trail of Tears tribes.
Identify the two kinds of waves produced by an earthquake and the mediums through which each can travel.
1. Primary waves /P-waves - through solids & liquids; 2. secondary waves / S-waves - through solids only
P-waves come first and go through anything. S-waves are stopped by liquid — that's how we know the outer core is molten.
Identify the five most common chemical elements that make up living tissue and state their chemical symbol.
Oxygen, O; hydrogen, H; carbon, C; nitrogen, N; phosphorus, P
Water alone accounts for two of them. The other three are the backbone of every organic molecule, the one in every protein, and the one in DNA and bone. Metals and minerals miss the top five.

Identify which of the following has a density closest to steel: Object “A” has a mass of 54 g and a volume of 8 mL; Object “B” has a mass of 240 g and a volume of 25 mL; Object “C” has a mass of 95 g and a length of 5 cm and height of 2 cm and a width of 1 cm; Object “D” has a mass of 55 g and when placed in water the water rises from 52 mL to 59 mL. The density of steel is 7.81 g per cm cubed.
Object D is the closest with a density of 7.86 g/mL
Density is mass divided by volume. For D, the volume is how much the water rose.

Match the following Germans to what they are best known for: Matthias Goerne, Hans Holbein, Helmut Kohl, Albert Lortzing, Friedrich Schiller, Jan Ullrich, Christoph Waltz / Specialty: poet, actor, composer, singer, artist, politician, athlete
Matthias Goerne = singer; Hans Holbein = artist; Helmut Kohl = politician; Albert Lortzing = composer; Friedrich Schiller = poet; Jan Ullrich = athlete; Christoph Waltz = actor
Holbein painted Tudor portraits. Kohl reunified Germany. Ullrich won the Tour de France. Waltz won Oscars.

Determine how many degrees of a circle graph you would devote to each class in a pie chart showing time spent on homework, given the hours spent each week: math = 3 hours; English = 2.5 hours; history = 2 hours; science = 1.5 hours; other = 1 hour.
Ten hours total, and a circle is 360 degrees. So each hour is 36 degrees.
King Leonidas delayed a vastly larger Persian force under Xerxes I in a mountain pass whose name means “hot gates” at this 480 BCE battle.
Greek for “hot gates.” Three hundred Spartans held it.
Name the Roman emperor, successor to Trajan, known for his wall at the border between England and Scotland.
His wall still runs across northern England.
This Roman emperor, the successor to Trajan, is known for his wall at the border between England and Scotland.
Name the war where Florence Nightingale focused on the sanitary design of hospitals and became known as “The Lady with the Lamp.”
Fought in the 1850s, largely on a peninsula in the Black Sea.
In this war Florence Nightingale focused on the sanitary design of hospitals and became known as “The Lady with the Lamp.”
The Arkansas River begins in this mountainous state, where it flows through the steep Royal Gorge and past the city of Pueblo before entering the Great Plains. Name the state.
Its name is Spanish for “colored red,” which is also what the river is named for.
The Arkansas River begins in this mountainous state, flowing through the steep Royal Gorge and past the city of Pueblo before it reaches the Great Plains.
Name the North American mountain range that is named for the many waterfalls along the Columbia River Gorge.
Named for the falls. The range runs from northern California up through Oregon and Washington.
This North American mountain range is named for the many waterfalls along the Columbia River Gorge.
Name the 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against segregating public schools.
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
“Separate but equal” was struck down. The city is the capital of Kansas.
Cumming v. Richmond County Board of Education
In this 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against segregating public schools.
Name the 1966 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against Arizona policemen, who failed to read a suspect his rights.
You've heard the warning read on television. The state is Arizona.
In this 1966 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against Arizona policemen who failed to read a suspect his rights.
Name the 1896 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a New Orleans man seeking to integrate railway cars in Louisiana.
The case that made “separate but equal” legal in the first place.
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
In this 1896 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against a New Orleans man seeking to integrate railway cars in Louisiana.
Give the economic term that refers to a share of money earned by an investment or a business and then given to stockholders.
A share of the profits paid out to shareholders.
This economic term refers to a share of the money earned by an investment or a business and then given to stockholders.
Name the term economists use to describe the highest-valued alternative that must be given up in order to engage in a given activity.
What you give up is the cost of the choice you made. Two words.
Economists use this term for the highest-valued alternative that must be given up in order to engage in a given activity.
Give the business term that refers to a group of people who are allowed by law to run a company, college, or town as a single business.
A legal body treated as a single entity, separate from its owners.
This business term refers to a group of people who are allowed by law to run a company, college, or town as a single business.
Give the economic term that describes a factor that encourages or motivates a person to do or buy something.
A reward or a reason to act — the carrot, not the stick.
This economic term describes a factor that encourages or motivates a person to do or buy something.
Give the economic term used to describe something acquired with the intention to make money with it in the future.
Money put in now to make more money later.
This economic term describes something acquired with the intention of making money with it in the future.
What is the value of the expression 3x + 4y3 [3x plus 4y cubed] if x =3 and y= -2.
Substitute first: 3(3) + 4(−8). Watch the sign on the cube.
This is the value of the expression 3x + 4y³ when x = 3 and y = −2.
Shay is traveling at a rate of 75 miles per hour. How fast is Shay traveling in feet per second?
75 miles is 396,000 feet; an hour is 3,600 seconds. Or remember that 60 mph is 88 ft/s.
Shay is traveling 75 miles per hour, which comes to this speed in feet per second.
How many ways can the letters in FACTOR be arranged so that the first and last letters are vowels?
FACTOR has two vowels, A and O. They must take the first and last spots — in either order.
The letters in FACTOR can be arranged this many ways with a vowel first and last.
Convert the adjective “global” into an adverb.
Most adjectives take -ly. Watch the spelling: global already ends in l.
The adjective “global” turns into this adverb.
When used to describe a color, “orange” is an adjective. When used to describe a citrus fruit, what part of speech is it?
If the word names a thing you can hold, which part of speech is it?
“Orange” is an adjective when it describes a color; when it describes a citrus fruit it is this part of speech.
Words such as “these” or “those” used to specify nouns act as which parts of speech?
They point out which noun you mean, so they describe it.
Words such as “these” or “those,” used to specify nouns, act as these parts of speech.
Give an example of a preposition.
any word that would specify position
Any word showing where or when something sits relative to something else: under, near, before.
Give an example of a noun.
any word that would specify a person, place, thing or idea
Any person, place, thing, or idea.
Give an example of a verb.
any word that would specify action, including the to be verb
Any action word — or a form of “to be.”
Give an example of an adjective.
any word that would specify the description of a noun
Any word that describes a noun.
Give an example of an article, grammatically speaking.
There are only three: a, an, the.
Give an example of an interjection.
any word that would specify exclamation, i.e Wow! Yikes! Oops! Excellent! Awesome! Darn!
A word you shout on its own, usually with an exclamation mark.
Steven, Sally, and Samuel evenly split a total allowance of $120 for their four hours of yard work. How much did each receive and how much did they earn hourly?
each received $40; they received $10 per hour
$120 split three ways, over four hours each.
Pluralize the following singular nouns: goose, passerby, attorney general, octopus.
Two of these pluralize the first word, not the last. Goose is irregular.
Max worked five hours on Wednesday, two hours on Friday, and 55 minutes on Saturday. Gina worked four hours on Wednesday, 75 minutes on Friday, and two hours on Saturday. Who worked longer?
Convert everything to minutes before you compare.
Max worked five hours Wednesday, two hours Friday, and 55 minutes Saturday; Gina worked four hours Wednesday, 75 minutes Friday, and two hours Saturday. This one worked longer.
Which of the following plays were not written by William Shakespeare?: Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet, Death of a Salesman, King Lear, Julius Caesar, and The Crucible
Death of a Salesman and The Crucible
Two of these are twentieth-century American plays by Arthur Miller.
Matt ordered three feet of yellow yarn, eight feet of green yarn, and nine feet of purple yarn. How many inches of yarn did Matt order?
Twenty feet of yarn altogether, and twelve inches per foot.
Matt ordered three feet of yellow yarn, eight feet of green, and nine feet of purple — this many inches in all.
Christine ran 24 laps around her high school track. Each lap was .25 miles long. How many miles did Christine run?
A quarter mile per lap, 24 laps.
Christine ran 24 laps of her high school track at .25 miles a lap, covering this distance.
Name the only two United States capitals that rhyme.
Both end in the same two syllables. One is in Massachusetts, one in Texas.
These are the only two United States capitals that rhyme.
As of the 2020 census, what US state had a population greater than the entire population of Canada?
About 39 million people at the 2020 census, more than all of Canada at the time.
As of the 2020 census, this US state had a population greater than the entire population of Canada.
Name the economic term that describes consumer desire and means to purchase goods and services at a given price.
The buyers' side of the market.
This economic term describes consumer desire and the means to purchase goods and services at a given price.
Name the economic term that describes a plan for spending and saving money used by individuals, businesses, or governments.
A plan for money coming in and going out.
This economic term describes a plan for spending and saving money, used by individuals, businesses, or governments.
Name the economic term used for a person who buys and/or uses goods and services.
The person at the end of the line who actually uses the product.
This economic term is used for a person who buys and/or uses goods and services.
Name the 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a segregating governmental body in Topeka, Kansas.
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
Topeka is the clue — the case is named for the school board there.
Cumming v. Richmond County Board of Education
In this 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against a segregating governmental body in Topeka, Kansas.
Name the 1963 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against the state of Florida, which argued that the state only needed to provide lawyers to defendants in death penalty cases.
The right to a lawyer, even if you can't pay. The defendant's surname starts with G.
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
In this 1963 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against the state of Florida, which argued it only had to provide lawyers to defendants in death penalty cases.
Name the 1944 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a Japanese man who claimed internment during World War II violated his 5th Amendment rights.
Japanese American internment during World War II. The name is Japanese.
In this 1944 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against a Japanese man who claimed internment during World War II violated his 5th Amendment rights.
Name the 1919 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a socialist pamphleteer exercising unpopular free speech rights during World War I.
“Clear and present danger” came from this case.
In this 1919 U.S. Supreme Court case the majority ruled against a socialist pamphleteer exercising unpopular free speech rights during World War I.
The sedimentary rock shale becomes what metamorphic rock?
Squeeze mud-rock and it splits into flat sheets — good for roofs and chalkboards.
The sedimentary rock shale becomes this metamorphic rock.
The sedimentary rock sandstone becomes what metamorphic rock?
Squeeze sand grains together hard and they fuse into a very hard rock.
The sedimentary rock sandstone becomes this metamorphic rock.
Name the type of rock that makes up the ocean floor.
Dark, fine-grained volcanic rock — the same stuff Hawaii is made of.
This type of rock makes up the ocean floor.
Name the type of rock that includes limestone.
Limestone is made of shells and sediment pressed together.
Limestone is this type of rock.
Name the type of metamorphic rock that limestone becomes.
Newton’s 1st Law of Motion is also known as the law of what?
An object keeps doing what it's doing. One word, starting with I.
Newton’s 1st Law of Motion goes by this other name.
Name the atmospheric layer that contains the ozone layer.
The layer that protects us from UV, sitting just above the one where weather happens.
This atmospheric layer contains the ozone layer.
In which layer of the atmosphere does weather occur?
The lowest layer — the one we live in.
Weather occurs in this layer of the atmosphere.
Natural selection can also be referred to by what phrase?
Darwin's idea, in four words, coined by Herbert Spencer.
Natural selection goes by this phrase as well.
Give the word deriving from ancient Persian that, as an adjective, can describe a color or, as a noun, a fruit.
The fruit and the color share one word.
This word, from ancient Persian, describes a color as an adjective and names a fruit as a noun.
Give the word deriving from Turkish that, as a noun, can describe a blue-green mineral often used in jewelry or, as an adjective, a color similar to that of the mineral.
Named after Turkey — the French called it “Turkish stone.”
This word, from Turkish, names a blue-green mineral often used in jewelry and, as an adjective, a color much like it.
Give the word of Persian origin that, as a noun, can describe a flower grown from bulbs or, as an adjective, varying shades of a ruby-red color.
The flower's name comes from the Persian word for turban, which it resembles.
This word of Persian origin names a flower grown from bulbs and, as an adjective, varying shades of ruby-red.
Give the noun of Turkish origin that describes a container for archery ammunition. As an English-derived verb, it can describe a shaking or trembling motion.
An archer carries one on their back — and it's also what you do when you shiver.
This noun of Turkish origin is a container for archery ammunition; as an English-derived verb it describes a shaking or trembling motion.
This word derives from Arabic and described a demon that ate human flesh. Give the word that in our time describes someone who enjoys gruesome stories or details.
Starts with G. Think of a gruesome, grave-robbing appetite.
This word comes from Arabic, where it described a demon that ate human flesh; today it describes someone who enjoys gruesome stories or details.
Give the meaning of the Greek root “astro” as used in words like “astronaut” and “astrolabe”.
Accept “star” or “stars” or “outer space” or related descriptions
Give the meaning of the Greek root “cycl” as used in words like “bicycle” and “cyclone”.
Bicycle wheels, a cyclone's spin, a cycle that comes around again.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “frag” or “fract” as used in words like “fragment” and “fracture”.
A fragment is a broken piece; a fracture is a broken bone.
Give the meaning of the Latin root “juven” as used in words like “juvenile” and “rejuvenate”.
Juvenile means young; to rejuvenate is to make young again.
Give the term used in the field of genetics that refers to an organism’s appearance.
Pheno- means “showing.” It's the traits you can actually observe.
This genetics term refers to an organism’s appearance.
Name the phenomenon that is caused by the tilt of the Earth's rotational axis toward or away from the sun.
The Earth leans about 23.5 degrees, and that lean is why summer and winter happen.
The tilt of the Earth’s rotational axis toward or away from the sun causes this.
Name two of the four gas giant planets in our solar system.
Any two: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
The four outer planets, past the asteroid belt — the ones with no solid surface to stand on.
Name the type of energy that results solely from motion.
Energy of motion. From the Greek for “to move.”
This type of energy results solely from motion.
Give the classification that describes about 90 of the 118 elements on the Periodic Chart. They tend to be hard, shiny and have good electrical and thermal conductivity.
Most of the periodic table. Shiny, conduct heat and electricity.
This classification covers about 90 of the 118 elements on the Periodic Chart; they tend to be hard and shiny with good electrical and thermal conductivity.
Give the common classification that describes about a dozen elements on the Periodic Chart. They appear as metallic, but are brittle and have only fair electrical conductivity.
Between metals and nonmetals — the staircase elements like silicon.
This classification covers about a dozen elements on the Periodic Chart; they look metallic but are brittle and only fair conductors of electricity.
Of metals, metalloids or nonmetals, which make up most living organisms?
Think about what living tissue is actually built from — the light elements, not the heavy ones.
Of metals, metalloids and nonmetals, these make up most living organisms.
Calculate the average of the integers from 13 to 31, inclusive.
There are 19 integers from 13 to 31, and they're evenly spaced. The average is the middle one.
This is the average of the integers from 13 to 31, inclusive.
Name the type of energy that is the sum of its kinetic and potential energy.
Kinetic plus potential. The word means “of machines.”
This type of energy is the sum of an object’s kinetic and potential energy.
Waves of energy bend when they move around obstructions or pass through narrow openings. Name this type of bending.
Bending around an edge or through a slit. Starts with D.
Waves of energy bend when they move around obstructions or pass through narrow openings, and this is the name for that bending.
Give the term that describes the very bright center of distant galaxies.
Extremely bright, extremely distant, powered by a black hole. Starts with Q.
This term describes the very bright center of distant galaxies.
Name the term for a sudden, intense brightening from a small area of the Sun's surface.
A sudden bright flash on the sun's surface.
This is the term for a sudden, intense brightening from a small area of the Sun’s surface.
Calculate the probability that exactly two heads will be showing if three coins are simultaneously flipped. Express your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
Eight equally likely outcomes for three coins. Count the ones with exactly two heads.
As a fraction in simplest form, this is the probability that exactly two heads show when three coins are flipped at once.
Calculate the volume of a rectangular box in cubic centimeters if it measures 5 mm × 10 mm × 1 m.
Convert everything to centimeters first: 0.5 cm × 1 cm × 100 cm.
In cubic centimeters, this is the volume of a rectangular box measuring 5 mm × 10 mm × 1 m.
Calculate the percent probability that a randomly selected multiple of 3 less than or equal to 3000 is also a multiple of 5.
Multiples of 3 that are also multiples of 5 are multiples of 15. So one in every five.
This is the percent probability that a randomly selected multiple of 3 less than or equal to 3000 is also a multiple of 5.
Four friends are going to eat lunch at a table with 6 chairs. Calculate the number of seating arrangements for the four friends.
Four friends, six chairs, and it matters who sits where. That's 6 × 5 × 4 × 3.
Four friends sit down to lunch at a table with 6 chairs, giving this many seating arrangements.
Anna’s mother has four daughters. One is named April, one is named May, and one is named June. Determine the name of the fourth daughter.
Read the very first word of the question again.
Anna’s mother has four daughters; one is named April, one May, and one June. This is the fourth.
Determine which word in the following list is least like the others: third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth.
Say each one out loud and listen to the ending.
Ninth is the only one over eight
Fifth is the only one with a v
Fourth is the only one that is a fraction
Of third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth and ninth, this word is the odd one out.
Complete the following syllogism – No reptiles have fur/All snakes are reptiles/Therefore….
If no reptile has fur, and every snake is a reptile, what follows?
No reptiles have fur. All snakes are reptiles. Therefore, this follows.
Complete this syllogism – Either it is slimy or it is not green/It is not both slimy and green/Therefore…

it is both slimy and green
it is green but not slimy

Calculate how many pieces that are exactly 5 inches long Sally can cut from a cord that is 7 feet long.
